policy:0.en: The Manager pinned a new notice above the register. 'Our store *policy* is clear,' he said, tapping the paper. 'No item leaves without a receipt.' Lin stood nearby, arms folded, watching me struggle with the printer. I had no idea how to make it print two copies at once.

policy:0.line: 'Our *policy* says every customer gets a printed receipt, no exceptions.'

concern:0.en: A small boy pressed his face against the glass door, staring at the row of canned drinks. His *concern* was written all over him — he was counting coins in his palm, lips moving quietly. I pretended to tidy the shelf nearest the door so I could keep a gentle eye on him.

concern:0.hook: He pocketed the coins and slowly walked away empty-handed.
concern:0.line: 'My only *concern* is whether he has enough money for that drink.'

present:0.en: Tang arrived early for the handover and set a small paper bag on the counter. 'A little *present* for surviving your first week,' she said, grinning. Inside was a travel-size bottle of eye drops and a pack of coffee candy. It was the most practical gift anyone had ever given me.
present:0.cnHint: 唐提前来交班，给我带了一份小____，里面装着眼药水和咖啡糖。
present:0.hook: At the bottom of the bag was a folded, unsigned note.

claim:0.en: Lin dropped a loyalty card on the counter and crossed her arms. 'I want to *claim* my free coffee,' she said flatly. I checked the card — nine stamps, all slightly different shades of ink. The tenth box was stamped too, but the ink looked fresh, almost wet. I hesitated, pen in hand.
claim:0.cnHint: 林拿着集点卡来____免费咖啡，但那第十个印章看起来墨水还没干。

half:0.en: It was *half* past two in the morning when the store went completely silent. No cars, no footsteps, not even the hum of a passing bike. I stood behind the counter eating a rice ball, listening to the ceiling light buzz softly. Then the door sensor beeped — but no one came in.
half:0.cnHint: 凌晨____两点，店里安静得出奇，门感应器突然响了却没有人进来。
half:0.hook: A shadow passed slowly across the frosted glass panel.
half:0.line: 'It is *half* past two — who on earth shops at this hour?'

successful:0.en: Lin set her tablet on the counter and showed me a graph. 'My trial promotion last month was *successful*,' she said, zooming in on a rising line. 'Sales up eighteen percent.' The Manager had asked her to test a buy-two-get-one deal, and she had clearly nailed it. I felt a quiet, uncomfortable mix of admiration and dread.
successful:0.cnHint: 林展示了她上个月促销活动的____成果，销售额上升了18%。
successful:0.hook: She then looked at me and said, 'Your turn next week.'
successful:0.line: 'The buy-two-get-one trial was *successful* beyond what anyone expected.'

access:0.en: I reached for the back-room door and found it locked. 'You don't have *access* to that area yet,' the Manager called from across the store, not even turning around. I wondered what was kept in there — extra stock, old records, or something else entirely. The keypad blinked a slow, patient red.
access:0.cnHint: 我发现自己还没有后室的____权限，店长头也没回地提醒了我。

positive:0.en: Lin walked in at midnight, arms crossed, eyes sharp. She ran the rival shop two blocks away. 'Your snack wall is a mess,' she said. But then she paused at the new display I had just built. Her silence felt oddly *positive*, like a teacher holding back a smile.
positive:0.cnHint: 林来店里视察，对新展示架的反应出乎意料地____。
positive:0.hook: She left without a word, but she glanced back once.
positive:0.line: 'I try to stay *positive*, even when the competition is tough.'

economic:0.en: Lin dropped a thick folder on the counter. 'Look at these numbers,' she said. She had tracked every *economic* shift on this street for three years — rent, foot traffic, snack trends. I stared at the charts. She was not just a rival. She was something closer to an expert.
economic:0.cnHint: 林拿出数据，分析这条街的____变化。
economic:0.hook: The last page had our store's name circled in red ink.
economic:0.line: 'Every small shop feels the *economic* pressure these days.'

link:0.en: Lin pointed at the shelf where our drinks sat next to hers — same brand, same price. 'There is a clear *link* between what you stock and what I stock,' she said quietly. I had not noticed until now. Someone was supplying us both, and maybe that was not a coincidence.
link:0.cnHint: 林发现两家店的货源之间有某种____。
link:0.hook: She pulled out a delivery receipt that matched ours exactly.
link:0.line: 'That *link* between our suppliers — did you know about it?'

produce:0.en: The back room was warm and smelled of cardboard. Lin stood watching as I stacked boxes. 'A small store like this can *produce* a real sense of community,' she said, almost to herself. It was the kindest thing she had ever said to me, and it landed softly in the quiet night.
produce:0.cnHint: 林在库房里说，小店能____真正的社区归属感。
produce:0.hook: Then she asked if she could borrow our storage space.

teach:0.en: Lin sat on the stool behind the counter — my stool — and began to sort coins faster than I could follow. 'Watch,' she said. 'I will *teach* you the quick count.' Her fingers were a blur. I leaned in close, suddenly grateful for a rival who did not mind sharing a secret.
teach:0.cnHint: 林坐下来，决定____我一个收银小技巧。
teach:0.hook: She stopped mid-lesson and looked at the door with narrowed eyes.
teach:0.line: 'Let me *teach* you one thing that took me a year to learn.'

worth:0.en: Lin picked up our new premium rice ball, turned it over, and read the price tag. She set it down slowly. 'That is *worth* the money,' she said, with the careful tone of someone who does not give praise easily. I felt the compliment settle in my chest like warm tea.
worth:0.cnHint: 林拿起我们的新饭团，认为它____这个价钱。
worth:0.hook: She bought two, paid in exact change, and said nothing more.

daily:0.en: Lin unfolded a small notebook filled with neat rows of numbers. She tracked her *daily* sales in pencil, every single entry written by hand. 'Digital records can disappear,' she said simply. The notebook was soft at the edges from months of use. I had never thought a rival could feel so familiar.
daily:0.cnHint: 林展示她手写的____销售记录本。
daily:0.hook: The last entry had today's date but tomorrow's figures.
daily:0.line: 'My *daily* record keeps me honest with myself.'

determine:0.en: Lin walked in at midnight, set three different energy drinks on the counter, and asked me to taste each one. 'I need to *determine* which sells best before the Manager orders more stock,' she said. Her notebook was already open, pen ready. She looked more like a scientist than a store clerk.
determine:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林让我试喝三种饮料，想____哪种最畅销。
determine:0.hook: But her pen stopped moving when she saw my face.
determine:0.line: 'I need to *determine* the best one before tomorrow morning.'

response:0.en: I asked Lin why she always rearranged the snack shelf at 2 a.m. She kept stacking chips in silence. My *response* to her silence was to stack them back the way they were. She turned around slowly, one eyebrow raised, and I suddenly felt I had made a very large mistake.
response:0.cnHint: 我对隔壁咖啡店的林沉默的____是把零食摆回原位，结果……
response:0.hook: She smiled, and that smile was harder to read than any silence.
response:0.line: 'Your *response* tells me everything I needed to know.'

search:0.en: Lin came in from the rain, shaking water off her jacket. She began a quiet *search* through every shelf near the door, picking up items and putting them down. 'Lost something?' I asked. She looked up, paused, and said only, 'Not yet.'
search:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林冒雨进店，在货架间____着什么，却说'还没丢'。
search:0.hook: She left without buying anything, but her eyes swept the door twice.
search:0.line: 'My *search* always starts here, at this shelf.'

regard:0.en: The Manager once told me to *regard* Lin as a rival, but after she quietly covered my register when I knocked over a whole tray of coins, I was not so sure. She said nothing about it afterward. Tang saw the whole thing and gave me a slow, knowing nod.
regard:0.cnHint: 店长叫我把隔壁咖啡店的林____对手，但她悄悄帮了我一个忙。
regard:0.hook: Tang's nod suggested this was not the first time Lin had done that.
regard:0.line: 'You should *regard* her more carefully before you decide anything.'

true:0.en: Tang told me the *true* reason Lin always chose the window seat to eat her late snack: from there she could see the reflection of every shelf in the glass. She missed nothing. 'She is studying this store,' Tang said quietly, 'the way a student studies before a very big exam.'
true:0.cnHint: 阿糖告诉我隔壁咖啡店的林坐窗边的____原因，原来她一直在观察整家店。
true:0.hook: I looked at the window and saw my own reflection staring back, surprised.
true:0.line: 'The *true* reason is something only I have noticed, until now.'

depend:0.en: Whether the night shift felt long or short seemed to *depend* entirely on whether Lin stopped by. On quiet nights without her, every minute stretched like taffy. On nights she came in arguing cheerfully about shelf space with Tang, the hours were gone before I noticed.
depend:0.cnHint: 夜班时间过得快不快，全____隔壁咖啡店的林会不会来店里。
depend:0.hook: Tonight she was already twenty minutes later than usual.
depend:0.line: 'Everything here seems to *depend* on habits nobody admits to having.'

expensive:0.en: Lin held up a small jar of imported honey and turned it over to read the price. 'This is *expensive*,' she said, but she placed it in her basket without blinking. Tang leaned over to me and whispered, 'She buys one every week. She just likes to say that first.'
expensive:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林每次都说蜂蜜太____，却每周都买一罐。
expensive:0.hook: This week she picked up two jars, not one.
expensive:0.line: 'It is *expensive*, yes — and I will take it anyway.'

explain:0.en: Lin walked in just before midnight, arms crossed, eyes sharp. She set a notebook on the counter and tapped it twice. 'Your stock list is wrong,' she said. I asked her to *explain*. She opened the notebook and began reading out numbers, calm and precise, like a teacher grading a test.
explain:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林把账本放在柜台上，要求我____她指出的库存问题。
explain:0.hook: Every number she read matched a gap I had not noticed yet.
explain:0.line: 'Just *explain* to me why the milk count is wrong.'

examine:0.en: Lin pulled a carton of juice from the shelf and held it under the light. She turned it slowly, reading every line of small text. 'You should always *examine* the goods before you shelve them,' she said, not unkindly. I nodded, quietly checking the next carton in my hand.
examine:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林拿起一盒果汁，仔细____包装上的每一行文字。
examine:0.hook: The carton in my hand had a date that made my stomach drop.
examine:0.line: 'Always *examine* the goods before they go on the shelf.'

influence:0.en: Lin reorganised the snack shelf without asking. She put the cheap crackers at eye level and moved the pricey ones to the bottom. 'Position can *influence* what people buy,' she said simply. By two in the morning, three bags of the cheap crackers were already gone.
influence:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林调整了货架陈列，告诉我摆放位置会____顾客的购买选择。
influence:0.hook: She smiled at the empty shelf space like she had seen this before.
influence:0.line: 'Good display can *influence* what a customer picks up.'

argue:0.en: Lin said the store should close the side door at night to save heat. I said the Manager kept it open for the delivery driver. We began to *argue* in low voices, neither of us wanting to wake the one customer asleep over a cup of warm soup in the corner.
argue:0.cnHint: 我和隔壁咖啡店的林压低声音____要不要关上侧门，谁也不肯让步。
argue:0.hook: The sleeping customer stirred, muttered a single word, and went still again.
argue:0.line: 'I don't want to *argue*, but that door wastes heat all night.'

pass:0.en: It was nearly three when Tang asked me to *pass* the pricing gun across the counter. Lin watched from the doorway of the stock room, arms folded. 'He holds it wrong,' she said quietly. Tang looked at me and raised one eyebrow, as if to say: she is always watching.
pass:0.cnHint: 阿糖让我把打价签的工具____给他，隔壁咖啡店的林在旁边默默观察。
pass:0.hook: Lin stepped closer, and Tang gripped the pricing gun a little tighter.
pass:0.line: 'Can you *pass* me the pricing gun? I need to tag these.'

serious:0.en: Lin found a broken seal on a bag of rice near the back of the shelf. Her face went very *serious*. She pulled every bag forward and checked each one by hand, lining the checked bags neatly on the floor. No one asked her to do it. She just did it.
serious:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林发现一袋米封口破损，神情变得十分____，开始逐一检查。
serious:0.hook: When she reached the last bag, she paused for just a moment too long.
serious:0.line: 'This is *serious*. A broken seal means the product is unsafe.'

despite:0.en: The heating unit made a loud clank at midnight. *Despite* the cold air creeping in from the gap under the door, Lin stayed at the counter working through her notebook without a coat, her pen moving steadily across the page. I offered her a hot canned drink. She accepted without looking up.
despite:0.cnHint: 尽管____寒意阵阵，隔壁咖啡店的林依然在柜台边专注地翻看她的笔记本。
despite:0.hook: She paused, circled something on the page, and said nothing.
despite:0.line: '*Despite* the cold, I want to finish checking this before morning.'

express:0.en: I filled the shelf wrong again. I could see Lin wanted to say something sharp, but she paused, took a breath, and chose her words carefully. She tried to *express* her point without making me feel small. It almost worked. Her eyebrow still went up just a little at the end.
express:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林想____自己的不满，但她努力控制语气，尽量说得温和。
express:0.hook: That slight eyebrow lift stayed in my mind for the rest of the shift.
express:0.line: 'Let me *express* this kindly: the heavier cans go on the bottom row.'

conduct:0.en: Lin walked in just before midnight and stood by the snack shelf for ten minutes without picking anything up. The Manager had warned me about this. 'Watch how Lin *conducts* herself near the new displays,' he had said. I watched. She was studying our shelf layout, cool and careful, like a general reading a map.
conduct:0.cnHint: 林在零食货架旁的____让店长早有预料。
conduct:0.hook: She photographed the price tags before I could say a word.
conduct:0.line: 'I always *conduct* my research before making any move.'

reveal:0.en: Tang nudged me around 2 a.m. and pointed at the security screen. Lin was standing outside, notebook in hand, sketching our window display. 'Don't let that *reveal* anything to her,' Tang whispered, quickly turning our new sign around. I had not even noticed the sign held our restock schedule.
reveal:0.cnHint: 唐不想让橱窗陈列向林____太多信息。
reveal:0.hook: The schedule was already half-copied into her notebook.
reveal:0.line: 'Never *reveal* your restock day — that is how rivals win.'

powerful:0.en: The Manager brewed his late-night tea and explained the store's history to me. 'Location is *powerful*,' he said, tapping the counter. 'Lin's shop is two blocks away, but people still walk past hers to reach ours.' I looked around at the warm light and the familiar smell and thought I was starting to understand why.
powerful:0.cnHint: 店长认为地理位置的____是我们胜过林的关键。
powerful:0.hook: Then he mentioned Lin had just signed a lease one block closer.
powerful:0.line: 'A good corner is more *powerful* than any discount campaign.'

push:0.en: Lin launched a late-night stamp-card deal, and suddenly our quiet hours felt quieter. Tang called it 'the *push*.' We had three customers between midnight and two; Lin's place, Tang reported, had eleven. The Manager just refilled the coffee machine and said we would answer with quality, not panic. I hoped he was right.
push:0.cnHint: 林发起了一轮____，让我们深夜的客流明显减少。
push:0.hook: By Thursday, two of our regulars were carrying Lin's stamp cards.
push:0.line: 'Every big *push* she makes just tells us where she feels weak.'

design:0.en: Lin stopped by just after 1 a.m. and asked, politely, if she could take a flyer from our rack. I said yes. Later, Tang pulled up a photo on his phone — Lin's new shelf layout. 'She didn't come for the flyer,' Tang said. 'She came to *design* her counter around ours.' I stared at the photo for a long time.
design:0.cnHint: 林来店里其实是为了____她自己店的新布局。
design:0.hook: Her new counter, Tang said, would open in four days.
design:0.line: 'Smart rivals *design* their spaces by studying yours first.'

exercise:0.en: Around 3 a.m. the store was empty, so Tang decided to *exercise* by doing slow lunges down the empty snack aisle. I was trying not to laugh when Lin appeared at the glass door, looked in, blinked, and walked away without entering. Tang straightened up immediately. 'She saw nothing,' he said with great dignity.
exercise:0.cnHint: 唐在店里____时被林撞见，场面颇为尴尬。
exercise:0.hook: Lin was back ten minutes later, this time with her phone camera ready.

space:0.en: The Manager decided to rearrange the store, pulling two shelves apart to create an open reading *space* with a single stool and a small lamp. 'People stay longer when they feel comfortable,' he said. I set up the stool carefully. By 4 a.m., a student was sitting there with a textbook, and the store felt like a different place entirely.
space:0.cnHint: 店长在店里开辟了一块____，希望让顾客多停留一会儿。
space:0.hook: The student looked up and said Lin's store had no such corner.
space:0.line: 'A little *space* like this changes how people feel about a shop.'

sign:0.en: The store had been quiet all evening, which was never a good *sign*. Then Lin walked in, looked around slowly, and pulled out a small notebook. She wrote something down, then smiled at me without saying a word. I felt a cold feeling in my chest.
sign:0.cnHint: 林走进店里四处打量，把什么记在本子上，这不是个好____。
sign:0.hook: Whatever she wrote in that notebook, I needed to see it.
sign:0.line: 'A quiet store at midnight is never a good *sign*,' Lin said softly.

feeling:0.en: Lin stood near the drinks shelf for a long time, moving nothing, saying nothing. I had a strange *feeling* that she was counting something — maybe our stock, maybe our prices. The Manager watched her too, pretending to fix a display. Nobody spoke first.
feeling:0.cnHint: 林在饮料架旁站了很久，我有一种奇怪的____，她在暗中记录什么。
feeling:0.hook: The Manager's smile looked a little too calm to be real.
feeling:0.line: 'I have a *feeling* you already know why I am here,' Lin said.

professional:0.en: Lin placed her own store's price list on our counter without asking. Everything about her was neat, careful, and very *professional* — her clothes, her voice, her small polite smile. The Manager thanked her as if it were a gift, then waited until she left to frown.
professional:0.cnHint: 林把她店里的价格表放在柜台上，举止十分____，让店长当场愣住了。
professional:0.hook: That price list had numbers that should have been impossible.
professional:0.line: 'We like to keep things *professional*,' Lin said, pushing the paper forward.

behind:0.en: I noticed it during the evening rush: our new drinks display was two weeks *behind* Lin's store, which had the same items up already. The Manager said nothing, but I saw him cross something off his planning list with a very hard press of the pen.
behind:0.cnHint: 我发现我们的新品陈列比林的店整整____了两周。
behind:0.hook: Something — or someone — was feeding Lin our plans early.
behind:0.line: 'You are always a little *behind* us,' Lin told the Manager, almost kindly.

government:0.en: Lin pointed at a small paper near our door. It was a new *government* notice about store hours that had arrived that morning. 'We put ours up yesterday,' she said quietly. I had not even opened the envelope yet. The Manager went pale.
government:0.cnHint: 林指着我们门口刚收到的____通知，说她的店昨天就贴出来了。
government:0.hook: If we had missed the deadline, the fine would be serious.
government:0.line: 'The *government* notice had a deadline,' Lin said, tapping the paper.

growth:0.en: Lin pulled up a small chart on her phone and held it toward the Manager. It showed her store's *growth* over the past three months — more customers, more sales, a rising line that did not stop. 'Just sharing,' she said, and put her phone away again.
growth:0.cnHint: 林拿出手机上的图表，向店长展示她店铺近三个月的____曲线。
growth:0.hook: The Manager stared at the door long after Lin had gone.
growth:0.line: 'Our *growth* this season has been quite satisfying,' Lin said with a smile.

negative:0.en: Lin read one of our customer review cards aloud — someone had written something *negative* about the store's lighting. She did not laugh. She just set the card back down gently and said we might want to think about it. Somehow that was worse than laughing.
negative:0.cnHint: 林大声念出一张对我们店有____评价的顾客留言卡。
negative:0.hook: I wondered how she had even known the card was there.
negative:0.line: 'I never enjoy leaving a *negative* review,' Lin said, almost to herself.

potential:0.en: Lin paused at our small empty shelf near the door. 'That corner has a lot of *potential*,' she said, as if thinking out loud. 'We use ours for local snacks. Very popular.' She gave a small nod and left. I stared at the empty shelf for a long time after.
potential:0.cnHint: 林看着我们门口空着的货架，说那个角落很有____，然后就走了。
potential:0.hook: By morning, I had three ideas — and no idea which one Lin had already tried.
potential:0.line: 'That space has real *potential*,' Lin said, nodding at our empty shelf.

real:0.en: Lin walked in just after midnight, glancing around like she was checking every shelf. 'So you're the new clerk,' she said, hands in her pockets. I smiled back, unsure if her friendliness was *real* or just a test. The Manager had warned me about her. I kept smiling anyway.
real:0.cnHint: 林深夜走进便利店，对新店员的友好态度让人摸不透是否出于____。
real:0.hook: Her eyes lingered one second too long on the register.
real:0.line: 'I need to know if this friendliness is *real* or just an act.'

talk:0.en: Lin leaned against the snack aisle and started a *talk* about store hours, pricing, and which clerk the regular customers preferred. talk:0.cnHint: 林在零食货架旁主动和新店员展开____，话题处处暗藏玄机。
talk:0.hook: She pulled out a small notebook before she left.
talk:0.line: 'This *talk* has been very useful — for me, at least.'

energy:0.en: Lin arrived carrying two large paper bags and began rearranging the cold-drinks section with quick, practiced hands. energy:0.cnHint: 林不是今晚的值班员，却带着惊人的____来整理冷饮区。

plan:0.en: Lin spread a hand-drawn map of the store across the front counter and explained her *plan* to reorganise the layout before the weekend rush. Every detail had been measured. plan:0.cnHint: 林在柜台上展开手绘地图，详细说明她改造店铺的____。
plan:0.hook: She said the Manager had already signed off on everything.
plan:0.line: 'My *plan* will double the impulse-buy rate — just watch.'

bear:0.en: By two in the morning the store felt very small. Lin had catalogued every item I had mis-shelved during my first week. I listened quietly, trying to *bear* the list with a straight face. There were fourteen items. She read them all twice. The fluorescent light above us buzzed like a tiny referee.
bear:0.cnHint: 林把新店员第一周所有的摆放失误都列了出来，看他能否____这份清单。

organization:0.en: Lin pointed at the storage room and shook her head slowly. 'This place has no *organization*,' she said, stepping over a box of instant noodles. She was not wrong. organization:0.cnHint: 林走进储物间，批评整个仓库缺乏____。
organization:0.hook: She offered to fix it in exchange for one favour.
organization:0.line: 'Good *organization* back here would save everyone ten minutes a day.'

opportunity:0.en: A delivery arrived at three in the morning, which meant I had to sign forms, stack boxes, and update the inventory screen — all at once. Lin watched from the magazine rack. 'This is your *opportunity* to show the Manager you can handle pressure,' she said. It was hard to tell if she was helping or enjoying herself.
opportunity:0.cnHint: 凌晨三点货物抵达，林告诉新店员这是一次难得的____。
opportunity:0.hook: She picked up a clipboard and began checking boxes herself.
opportunity:0.line: 'Treat every night rush as an *opportunity*, not a problem.'

professor:0.en: A tired man in a thick coat came in just before four and bought three cups of instant noodles. Lin greeted him by name. 'He's a *professor* from the college two blocks away,' she whispered to me after he left. 'Grades papers all night. Always pays exact change.' She said it like a small, proud fact she owned.
professor:0.cnHint: 一位深夜买泡面的顾客原来是附近大学的____，林对他了如指掌。
professor:0.hook: She knew the exact course he taught without being asked.
professor:0.line: 'That *professor* has bought the same noodles every night for two years.'

force:0.en: Lin walked in at 2 a.m. and started rearranging our snack display without asking. I told her this was my section. She smiled and said nobody could *force* her to leave a store that was open to everyone. The Manager would hear about this in the morning.
force:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林半夜闯入零食区，声称没人能____她离开。
force:0.hook: She picked up our best-selling item and raised one eyebrow.
force:0.line: Nobody can *force* me out of a public store, night clerk.

importance:0.en: Tang pulled me aside near the back fridge and whispered about the *importance* of keeping the milk section fully stocked before the morning rush. I had no idea a few missing cartons could cause such trouble. Apparently last Tuesday things got ugly.
importance:0.cnHint: 阿糖悄悄提醒我，牛奶区补货的____不容忽视。
importance:0.hook: Then Tang glanced toward the door and went very quiet.
importance:0.line: Never underestimate the *importance* of a full milk shelf.

sell:0.en: Lin slid a leaflet across the counter. Her family's shop down the road was running a big sale, and the leaflet was designed to *sell* the idea that fresher goods waited just fifty steps away. I stared at it. She was handing this out inside our store.
sell:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在我们店里散发传单，想____竞争对手的促销活动。
sell:0.hook: The Manager's office light flickered on.
sell:0.line: This leaflet will *sell* my shop better than any window sign.

replace:0.en: I noticed the price tag on the soy-milk shelf was wrong. Tang told me to *replace* it quickly before Lin spotted the mistake and took a photo for some reason none of us fully understood yet. I grabbed the correct tag and moved fast. Too late, maybe.
replace:0.cnHint: 价格标签出错，阿糖催我赶紧____它，免得隔壁咖啡店的林拍照。
replace:0.hook: Lin's phone was already halfway out of her pocket.
replace:0.line: *Replace* that tag right now, or we'll never hear the end of it.

approach:0.en: Lin's usual *approach* to visiting our store was simple: arrive, criticise the layout, leave. Tonight she tried something new. She stood at the magazine rack for twenty minutes without saying a word, just reading. That silence felt stranger than any complaint she had ever made.
approach:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林平时____我们店的方式是批评后离开，但今晚她只是沉默地站着。
approach:0.hook: She folded a page corner down very carefully.
approach:0.line: My new *approach* is to observe before I comment, clerk.

engage:0.en: The Manager had warned me that Lin liked to *engage* customers in conversation and subtly guide them toward her family's shop. So when I saw her chatting with our regular old gentleman near the hot-food counter, I drifted over and offered him a free sample.
engage:0.cnHint: 店长提醒我，隔壁咖啡店的林喜欢____顾客聊天，把他们引去别处。
engage:0.hook: The old gentleman looked at both of us and grinned slowly.
engage:0.line: I simply *engage* people in friendly talk — nothing wrong with that.

ensure:0.en: Before Lin could meddle with the new yoghurt display I had just built, I taped a small note to the shelf edge. It read: staff only. Tang said a note alone would not *ensure* anything, but it was the only tool I had at two in the morning.
ensure:0.cnHint: 为了____隔壁咖啡店的林不破坏我摆好的酸奶陈列，我贴了一张便条。
ensure:0.hook: Lin read the note, smiled, and reached past it anyway.
ensure:0.line: A little sign won't *ensure* anything, trust me on that.

limit:0.en: Tang told me there was a store rule: any single customer could only take two of the discounted instant noodles. Lin placed six on the counter without blinking. I pointed to the sign. She said the *limit* was a suggestion, not a law, and waited to see what I would do.
limit:0.cnHint: 促销泡面每人限购两包，隔壁咖啡店的林却拿了六包，声称____只是建议。
limit:0.hook: My hand hovered over the phone to call the Manager.
limit:0.line: A posted *limit* is just a suggestion if nobody enforces it.

video:0.en: The Manager called me over to a small screen near the back office. He wanted to show me something from last night. 'Watch this,' he said, pressing play. The *video* showed Lin standing at the snack shelf for nearly ten minutes, checking her phone between glances. I had no idea she had been here before I started.
video:0.cnHint: 店长让我看一段____，里面是林昨晚在零食架旁站了很久。
video:0.hook: Then the Manager pointed to something just out of frame.
video:0.line: 'This *video* was recorded the night before you joined us.'

prevent:0.en: Tang noticed that the front door had been left unlocked all evening. Anyone could have walked in and taken things from the shelf near the entrance. She quickly moved the most expensive items to a safer spot. 'We need to *prevent* this from happening again,' she said, already looking for a better lock in the back room.
prevent:0.cnHint: 汤发现大门整晚没锁，赶紧把贵重商品移走，说要____这种事再发生。
prevent:0.hook: Lin appeared at the door just as Tang turned the new lock.
prevent:0.line: 'We must *prevent* any more losses this week, okay?'

source:0.en: A regular customer brought in a small bag of homemade cookies and left them on the counter as a gift. Tang broke one open and looked thoughtful. 'These taste like the ones my grandmother made,' she said softly. I asked where the recipe came from. 'That old lady near the park,' she said. 'She is the *source* of half the good food in this neighbourhood.'
source:0.cnHint: 一位常客带来自制饼干，汤说附近那位老奶奶才是这一带美食的____。
source:0.hook: The bag had a small handwritten note none of us had noticed.
source:0.line: 'She is the *source* of every good recipe around here.'

available:0.en: I tried to find a spare key for the stockroom, but the hook on the wall was empty. I asked Tang, who shrugged. I asked the Manager, who checked his pockets twice. 'There is only one key *available*,' he said at last, 'and Lin borrowed it yesterday.' He said her name the way people say the word trouble.
available:0.cnHint: 库房备用钥匙不见了，店长说目前只有一把____的钥匙，被林借走了。
available:0.hook: Lin had not returned the key, and her phone was off.
available:0.line: 'There is only one key *available*, and she has it.'

customer:0.en: Just after two in the morning, a tired man came in and bought a hot drink and a small rice ball. He sat on the step outside for a while, then came back to return the empty cup. 'Thank you,' he said quietly. He was the kind of *customer* who made the night shift feel worthwhile. Then I noticed Lin watching him from across the street.
customer:0.cnHint: 凌晨两点，一位归还空杯的____让夜班变得有意义，但林却在街对面盯着他看。
customer:0.hook: The man glanced back at Lin and seemed to recognise her.
customer:0.line: 'Every *customer* deserves a warm place to rest a moment.'

language:0.en: Lin came in and began talking to the Manager in a fast, low voice. I could not follow along. Tang leaned close and whispered, 'They grew up in the same town. They use the local *language* when they do not want others to understand.' I smiled and pretended to restock the shelf, but I was listening very hard to the rise and fall of words I could not name.
language:0.cnHint: 林和店长用家乡____交谈，汤悄悄告诉我，他们是在不想让人听懂时才这样说话。
language:0.hook: Both of them looked at me at exactly the same moment.
language:0.line: 'We use this *language* only when something serious is happening.'

test:0.en: Tang set three unmarked cups of tea on the counter and asked me to guess which one came from the new supplier. 'This is a *test*,' she said, grinning. I tasted each one slowly. I chose the middle cup. Tang shook her head. 'Lin suggested this test,' she added, which somehow made getting it wrong feel much worse.
test:0.cnHint: 汤摆出三杯茶让我猜哪杯来自新供应商，说这是一次____，而这个主意是林出的。
test:0.hook: Tang poured the cups away before I could try again.
test:0.line: 'Lin said a *test* like this would show who really pays attention.'

save:0.en: Lin dropped a folded paper on the counter. 'I *save* every receipt from this store,' she said, patting a thick notebook. 'Three years of data.' She tapped her temple and smiled. I stared at the notebook. That was not a shopping habit. That was a research project.
save:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林把每张收据都____起来，厚厚一本，已经记录了三年。
save:0.hook: She turned back at the door and said, 'Your store has a pattern.'
save:0.line: 'I *save* every receipt — three years, not one missing.'

service:0.en: A woman in a heavy coat leaned over the counter. 'The *service* here used to be faster,' she said, not unkindly. Tang mouthed 'regulars' at me from behind the coffee machine. I smiled and handed her the change. She lingered, as if speed was never really the point.
service:0.cnHint: 一位常客对这里的____提出了意见，但似乎并不真的着急离开。
service:0.hook: She came back ten minutes later, just to stand near the heater.
service:0.line: 'The *service* here used to be faster, but I keep coming back.'

note:0.en: Lin left a small *note* under a bottle of green tea on the shelf. 'Wrong price tag — check your system.' I checked. She was right. The Manager just shrugged when I told him. 'She does that,' he said. 'Every Tuesday.'
note:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在货架上留了一张____，指出了标价的错误。
note:0.hook: I wondered how many other shelves she had already checked.
note:0.line: 'I left a *note* — your price tag has been wrong for a month.'

probably:0.en: A sleepy student shuffled in at two in the morning and stared at the hot-food shelf for a long time. 'This is *probably* my fourth visit today,' he said to no one. He picked up the same triangle rice snack as before. Tang gave me a look. We both knew it would not be his last.
probably:0.cnHint: 一个困倦的学生____是今天第四次来店里了。
probably:0.hook: He paused at the door and checked his phone with wide eyes.
probably:0.line: 'This is *probably* my fourth triangle snack today. Maybe fifth.'

strategy:0.en: Lin spread a small paper on the counter and asked if she could borrow a pen. 'New *strategy*,' she said cheerfully, drawing a rough map of the store layout. She marked the snack aisle with a circle. I handed her the pen without asking. Something told me I was part of her plan.
strategy:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在柜台上画图，说她有了新的____。
strategy:0.hook: The circle on her map was exactly where our newest display stood.
strategy:0.line: 'My new *strategy* starts with that snack aisle — watch.'

building:0.en: An old man pointed through the glass at the apartment *building* across the street. 'I have lived there forty years,' he said, setting down two cans of warm soup. 'This store is the best thing that ever happened to that corner.' He shuffled out. The street looked different after that.
building:0.cnHint: 一位老人指着对面的____，说这家店是这个街角最好的事。
building:0.hook: He left one can behind, label facing out, like a quiet thank-you.
building:0.line: 'That *building* has been there forty years, and so have I.'

community:0.en: The Manager taped a paper sign above the door: 'Lost-and-Found — ask inside.' He caught me reading it. 'We are a *community* here,' he said simply, and went back to his accounts. By midnight, three people had knocked to ask about a lost umbrella. It was the same umbrella every time.
community:0.cnHint: 店长说这家店是一个____，门口的失物招领告示引来了好几个人。
community:0.hook: The umbrella's owner never showed up, but someone else quietly claimed it.
community:0.line: 'This store is a *community* — I mean that seriously.'

internet:0.en: A teenage boy sat cross-legged on the floor by the magazine rack, phone held high. 'No signal,' he said miserably. 'Do you have *internet*?' Tang pointed to the small sign on the fridge: 'Wi-Fi — ask for password.' The boy's face lit up. He stayed two hours. He never bought anything. He did leave a five-star review.
internet:0.cnHint: 一个少年进来问有没有____，结果在店里待了两个小时。
internet:0.hook: His review mentioned the 'surprisingly welcoming floor space.'

stick:0.en: Lin walked in just before midnight and placed a handwritten sign on the shelf edge. 'Don't touch,' she said, pressing the corners down. The paper wouldn't *stick* to the cold metal — it kept sliding off — so she tried a second strip of tape, then a third, lips tight with concentration.
stick:0.cnHint: 林把一张手写告示____在货架边缘，但怎么也贴不牢。
stick:0.hook: Why did she need that sign up so badly?
stick:0.line: 'This label won't *stick*, so please hand me more tape.'

effective:0.en: Lin spent ten minutes rearranging the snack display near the door. 'Putting the popular items at eye level is more *effective*,' she told me, stepping back to check the result. The shelf did look tidier. I nodded, quietly wondering whether she was helping the store or simply making her own mark.
effective:0.cnHint: 林认为把商品放在视线高度是最____的陈列方式。
effective:0.hook: She seemed to know this store better than I did.
effective:0.line: 'A clear label is more *effective* than a fancy one, trust me.'

fear:0.en: A loud crash came from the stockroom. I froze at the counter, heart hammering. Lin appeared in the doorway a moment later, holding a fallen broom. She read the *fear* on my face and almost smiled. 'Relax,' she said. 'It is only a broom. The night is still young.'
fear:0.cnHint: 库房传来巨响，我脸上的____被林一眼看穿。
fear:0.hook: But her eyes darted once toward the back wall.
fear:0.line: 'Your *fear* shows — take a breath, it is just a broom.'

hit:0.en: Lin slid a bottle of water across the counter without looking up from her phone. It *hit* the small stand holding the receipt roll, and the roll bounced to the floor. She picked it up without a word, set it back, and returned to her screen as if nothing had moved at all.
hit:0.cnHint: 林推过来的水瓶____了收据架，纸卷滚落一地。
hit:0.hook: She had done exactly this before — I was sure of it.
hit:0.line: 'Did that bottle *hit* the stand? Sorry, I misjudged the distance.'

assume:0.en: I restocked the cup noodle shelf and left two gaps where the spicy flavour had sold out. Lin glanced over. 'Don't *assume* customers will ask — put a small sold-out tag there,' she said. It was practical advice. I cut a tag from spare card and slid it into the gap without argument.
assume:0.cnHint: 林提醒我不要____顾客会主动询问缺货情况，应贴上告示。
assume:0.hook: She had an answer ready before I even asked.
assume:0.line: 'Never *assume* customers will ask — always leave a clear tag.'

generally:0.en: Lin leaned on the end of the counter during a quiet spell. 'People *generally* go for the drink that is right at the front,' she said, nudging a row of cans forward a centimetre. 'Small push, big result.' I had been moving things all night without thinking about that at all.
generally:0.cnHint: 林说顾客____会拿摆在最前面的饮料，一厘米的距离就有大差别。
generally:0.hook: She nudged one more can forward and watched the door.
generally:0.line: 'Customers *generally* pick whatever is closest — so push it forward.'

interaction:0.en: A regular came in, greeted Lin by name, and they traded three quick jokes about the weather. When he left, Lin turned to me. 'Every *interaction* counts, even a small one,' she said, wiping the counter. 'He will be back tomorrow because of those thirty seconds.' I believed her.
interaction:0.cnHint: 林告诉我，与顾客的每一次____都很重要，哪怕只有三十秒。
interaction:0.hook: The regular paused at the door and looked back once.
interaction:0.line: 'A short *interaction* like that brings him back every time.'

top:0.en: Lin climbed the small step stool and set a ceramic cat on the *top* of the shelving unit near the window. She adjusted it until it faced the street. 'For good luck,' she said, climbing down. The cat's painted eyes caught the streetlight and seemed to watch every person who passed.
top:0.cnHint: 林把一只陶瓷猫摆在货架____，说是为了带来好运。
top:0.hook: No one had put anything up there before — until tonight.
top:0.line: 'Place it right on the *top* so everyone outside can see it.'

seek:0.en: Lin walked in just before midnight, eyes moving across every shelf. She was not buying anything. She seemed to *seek* some small weakness in how I arranged the drinks — a gap, a wrong price tag, anything she could report back to her own store. I smiled and asked if I could help.
seek:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在深夜来到便利店，似乎在____某种可以利用的破绽。
seek:0.hook: She paused at the back shelf and took out her phone.
seek:0.line: 'I always *seek* out the details other people miss,' Lin said quietly.

exist:0.en: I had worked three nights in a row and started to wonder if daytime still *existed* for me. The store felt like its own small world — bright lights, soft music, the hum of the fridge. Then Lin pushed open the door, looked around slowly, and I remembered: the outside world was still there, watching.
exist:0.cnHint: 我开始怀疑白天是否还____，直到隔壁咖啡店的林推门而入。
exist:0.hook: She was carrying a notebook, and she opened it the moment she sat down.
exist:0.line: 'Do you ever feel like nothing outside this store *exists* at night?' Lin asked.

supply:0.en: Tang pointed to the back room and said we were low on bottled water. I checked the shelves and saw he was right — only four bottles left. Our weekly *supply* had not arrived yet, and it was already Thursday. I called the Manager, who let out a long sigh on the other end.
supply:0.cnHint: 店里的瓶装水____不足，我赶紧联系店长。
supply:0.hook: The Manager's silence lasted just a little too long.
supply:0.line: 'The *supply* truck should have come yesterday,' Tang said, frowning at the shelf.

visit:0.en: The Manager stopped by at two in the morning — not a usual thing. He called it a quick *visit*, but he walked every aisle twice and checked the cooler temperature without saying a word. Tang and I exchanged a look. Something was being measured, though no one told us what.
visit:0.cnHint: 店长深夜突然____，在每条货架间来回走动。
visit:0.hook: Before he left, he photographed the front counter with his phone.
visit:0.line: 'This is just a friendly *visit*,' the Manager said, not quite smiling.

worry:0.en: Tang stayed ten minutes past the end of his shift, wiping the same counter twice. I asked him what was wrong. He said it was nothing, just a small *worry* about the monthly numbers. Sales had been quiet all week. He put the cloth down, said good night, and walked out into the dark street.
worry:0.cnHint: 阿糖下班后迟迟不走，心里有个小小的____。
worry:0.hook: He had left his jacket behind, which was not like him at all.
worry:0.line: 'It is only a small *worry*,' Tang said, 'but it will not leave me alone.'

adapt:0.en: My first week on the night shift was hard. Sleeping in the day felt wrong, eating at three in the morning felt wrong. But slowly I began to *adapt* — I learned which customers came at which hour, and the quiet started to feel almost comfortable. Then Lin arrived and made the quiet feel very different.
adapt:0.cnHint: 我慢慢开始____夜班的节奏，直到隔壁咖啡店的林的出现打破了宁静。
adapt:0.hook: She sat near the window and did not order anything for an hour.
adapt:0.line: 'You will *adapt* faster than you think,' the Manager told me on day one.

bit:0.en: Lin bought only a small bottle of green tea and a *bit* of hard candy — barely enough to fill one hand. She paid without looking at me, then sat at the little corner table by the window for the next forty minutes. I kept busy restocking chips, but I was watching her the whole time.
bit:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林只买了一点____糖果，却在角落里坐了将近一个小时。
bit:0.hook: She wrote something down each time a customer came through the door.
bit:0.line: 'Just a *bit* of candy, please,' Lin said, eyes still on the street outside.

check:0.en: Before the morning shift arrived, I had to *check* every price label in aisle two — Manager's orders. I was halfway through when I found one label that did not match the system. It was a small thing, but the number on it was exactly the number Lin had been photographing two nights before.
check:0.cnHint: 我奉命____第二排货架的价格标签，发现了一个奇怪的数字。
check:0.hook: The label had been placed there very recently — the edge was still clean.
check:0.line: 'Always *check* the labels in aisle two first,' the Manager had warned me.

easily:0.en: Lin walked in just before midnight, arms full of flyers for her own shop down the street. She dropped one on the counter without a word. I looked it over — cheaper prices, longer hours, friendlier photos. A customer who came in every night could *easily* switch sides without even noticing.
easily:0.cnHint: 林把她店铺的传单放在柜台上，上面的优惠条件让人觉得顾客____会被吸引走。
easily:0.hook: The flyer had our manager's photo crossed out in red.
easily:0.line: 'A regular could *easily* forget which store he actually likes.'

protect:0.en: The Manager had taped a small sign above the door: 'Staff only beyond this point.' Lin read it slowly, then smiled at me. 'He put that up yesterday,' Tang whispered from behind the shelves. 'To *protect* the back-room stock list. He thinks she memorises prices.'
protect:0.cnHint: 店长贴了一张告示，想____库存资料不被林看到。
protect:0.hook: Lin was already writing something in a small notebook.
protect:0.line: 'He just wants to *protect* the numbers she keeps asking about.'

advantage:0.en: Lin set up a small sample table just outside our door — free tea, tiny cups. By one in the morning, people were drinking her tea and then walking into our store. Tang nudged me. 'She gets all the warm feelings and we make all the sales. Who really has the *advantage* here?'
advantage:0.cnHint: 林在门口摆了免费茶水摊，但顾客喝完茶却走进了我们店，唐在想谁才有____。
advantage:0.hook: Lin refilled the teapot and smiled at the security camera.
advantage:0.line: 'Free tea outside gives me every *advantage* I need tonight.'

break:0.en: At two in the morning the store went quiet. Tang handed me a warm can of corn soup and pointed at the clock. 'Ten-minute *break*,' he said. 'Lin's shop has been dark for an hour. Even she needs sleep.' I sat on the step stool and felt, for one small moment, like we had won something.
break:0.cnHint: 深夜两点，唐让我休息一下，还指出林的店已经关灯——这短暂的____让人觉得轻松。
break:0.hook: Then Lin's lights flickered back on across the street.
break:0.line: 'Take a *break* — her store has finally gone dark.'

conclude:0.en: I watched Lin study our shelf layout for a full five minutes from the doorway. She counted the snack rows, checked the clock, and left without buying anything. Tang came to stand beside me. 'You can *conclude* one thing from all that looking,' he said quietly. 'She still hasn't found what makes us different.'
conclude:0.cnHint: 林在门口观察了很久又离开了，唐认为从她的行为可以____我们还有她不了解的东西。
conclude:0.hook: She came back twelve minutes later with a measuring tape.
conclude:0.line: 'You can *conclude* she still hasn't worked out our secret.'

figure:0.en: The Manager pinned a sheet of paper above the register before his shift ended. It showed one large *figure* circled in red: last week's midnight sales. He didn't explain it. He just tapped it twice with one finger, looked at me, and walked out. Tang appeared from the back room. 'Good number or bad number?' I asked.
figure:0.cnHint: 店长下班前把一个用红圈圈出的____贴在了收银台上方，没有任何解释。
figure:0.hook: Tang looked at it and immediately called the Manager back.
figure:0.line: 'That *figure* on the wall — do you know what it means?'

fit:0.en: Lin brought a small display stand and asked, very politely, if she could leave it near our entrance. 'Just for one night,' she said. The Manager looked at the stand, looked at our entrance, and shook his head slowly. 'It doesn't *fit* the space,' he said. The stand was exactly the right size. We all knew it.
fit:0.cnHint: 林想在我们店门口放她的展示架，店长说架子不____这个位置，但大家心里清楚这是借口。
fit:0.hook: Lin measured the space with her hand and said nothing.
fit:0.line: 'I checked — it will *fit* perfectly right by the door.'

particular:0.en: Tang had one rule about restocking: the bottom shelf on the left was always for a *particular* brand of instant noodles that one old regular bought every single night at three in the morning. No substitutions. No rearranging. I asked why. Tang just said, 'Some customers carry the whole mood of a night shift with them.'
particular:0.cnHint: 唐坚持为一位深夜常客在特定位置保留____品牌的泡面，不能随意替换。
particular:0.hook: That night, the old regular arrived and the shelf was empty.
particular:0.line: 'That *particular* shelf is not yours to rearrange, Lin.'

consequence:0.en: Lin walked in just after midnight, arms full of flyers. 'I am opening a new store across the street,' she said with a bright smile. The Manager stared at the flyers, then at me. I had no idea a rival store was even planned. The *consequence* for our quiet little shop could be serious.
consequence:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林带来了一个让店长震惊的消息，这件事的____可能影响到小店的未来。
consequence:0.hook: The Manager's coffee went cold as he kept staring at the door.
consequence:0.line: 'The *consequence* of doing nothing,' Lin said, 'is losing everything.'

realize:0.en: Lin dropped a thick folder of sales figures on the counter. I flipped through the pages slowly, comparing numbers from last month with this week. Then it hit me like a cold wind from the open door. I began to *realize* that our store was losing regular customers one by one, quietly, without anyone noticing.
realize:0.cnHint: 我翻看销售数据时，终于____到了一个令人不安的事实。
realize:0.hook: Tang leaned over and whispered, 'The Manager already knows.'
realize:0.line: 'Did you *realize* how many customers we lost this month?' Lin asked.

mostly:0.en: Lin spent an hour studying our snack shelves with a small notebook in hand. She wrote things down without a word. I asked what she was looking for. 'Your customers,' she said, 'are *mostly* students from the night class nearby.' She tapped her pen on the notebook. That felt less like a friendly observation and more like a plan.
mostly:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林仔细观察后，指出我们的顾客____是附近夜校的学生。
mostly:0.hook: She smiled and snapped the notebook shut before I could read a word.
mostly:0.line: 'Your buyers are *mostly* students, and I know exactly what students want.'

exactly:0.en: Lin pointed at our shelf of canned drinks and then at her own price list. 'Your cola is priced at three yuan,' she said. 'Mine is *exactly* the same.' She let that hang in the air. Tang crossed his arms. If the price was identical, we had nothing to offer that she did not — and she clearly knew it.
exactly:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林指出她新店的饮料价格与我们的____相同，这让阿糖很不安。
exactly:0.hook: Tang grabbed a marker and headed straight for the price tags.
exactly:0.line: 'My store charges *exactly* what you charge — so why would they stay?'

vary:0.en: Lin spread a colourful menu on the counter. 'My store will *vary* its hot food every week,' she said. 'Yours has sold the same three items for two years.' I looked at our small hot-food case — the same rice balls, the same egg rolls, the same fish cakes. She was not wrong, and that silence said everything.
vary:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林说她的新店会定期____热食种类，暗示我们的菜单太单调。
vary:0.hook: That night the Manager quietly pulled out a very old recipe book.
vary:0.line: 'I plan to *vary* the menu every single week to keep people curious.'

brain:0.en: It was nearly two in the morning when Lin sat at the small corner table with a large cup of tea and a pile of papers. She worked without stopping, filling pages with numbers and diagrams. Tang watched her from behind the magazine rack. 'That woman's *brain* never seems to rest,' he said to me in a low voice.
brain:0.cnHint: 阿糖看着深夜还在认真工作的隔壁咖啡店的林，感叹她的____从不停歇。
brain:0.hook: Lin glanced up from her papers as if she had heard every word.
brain:0.line: 'A good *brain* is the only tool you really need,' Lin said calmly.

stress:0.en: The Manager paced behind the counter all evening, checking the clock every few minutes. Lin had told him she would sign a lease on the shop across the street by Friday. The *stress* showed on his face — tight jaw, red eyes, untouched cup of tea. Tang slid him a fresh biscuit without saying anything. Sometimes that is enough.
stress:0.cnHint: 得知隔壁咖啡店的林即将在对面开店，店长承受着巨大的____，脸色很难看。
stress:0.hook: At midnight the Manager made a phone call he had been putting off for weeks.
stress:0.line: 'I feel the *stress* too,' Tang said quietly, 'but we will find a way.'

financial:0.en: Lin unfolded a single sheet of paper and placed it neatly on the counter. It was a simple table, but every number on it pointed the same way. 'Our *financial* position is stronger than yours right now,' she said, without any pride in her voice, just fact. I looked at the Manager. He nodded slowly, as if he had already known for a while.
financial:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林拿出数据，说明她的新店目前____实力比我们更强。
financial:0.hook: The Manager said nothing — but his hand was already reaching for the phone.
financial:0.line: 'My *financial* plan is ready,' Lin said. 'Is yours?'

fruit:0.en: Lin walked in just before midnight, carrying a small basket of *fruit* she had grown herself. She set it on the counter without a word. I waited. She finally said it was a gift — for whoever worked the night shift. I wondered why she looked so guilty.
fruit:0.cnHint: 林深夜带来一篮自己种的____，放在柜台上就想离开。
fruit:0.hook: But the note tucked inside was not for me.
fruit:0.line: 'I grew this *fruit* myself — please don't ask where.'

waste:0.en: Lin spent twenty minutes studying every label on the snack shelf. She picked up a bag, put it down, picked it up again. 'Don't *waste* your time reading those,' Tang said from behind the register. 'You already know what you want.' Lin froze and slowly turned around.
waste:0.cnHint: 林在货架前反复挑选零食，同事提醒她别____时间。
waste:0.hook: Tang's smile said he knew far more than he let on.
waste:0.line: 'It's not good to *waste* time on things that don't matter.'

learning:0.en: Lin came in every Tuesday with a thick notebook. She sat at the corner table, ordered hot tea, and never looked up. One night I asked what she was studying. She said it was not *learning* for school — it was something more personal, something she could not explain yet.
learning:0.cnHint: 林每周来店里做笔记，她说这种____不是为了考试。
learning:0.hook: She left the notebook behind that night.
learning:0.line: 'True *learning* starts when nobody is grading you.'

manager:0.en: A man in a neat jacket came in and stood very still near the door. Tang leaned over and whispered that he was the *manager* of the new shop opening across the street. Lin, restocking juice at the far end, went quiet. I watched her hands stop moving.
manager:0.cnHint: 一位新店的____走进来，林听到消息后动作突然停了下来。
manager:0.hook: He walked straight toward Lin without glancing at the shelves.
manager:0.line: 'The *manager* of that new shop has been asking about you.'

knowledge:0.en: Lin challenged me to name every product on the back wall without looking. I got about half right. She crossed her arms and said that in this kind of work, *knowledge* of your own shelves is the first thing that keeps customers coming back. I asked how long it took her to learn ours.
knowledge:0.cnHint: 林考了我一个关于货架的____小测试，结果让我有点难堪。
knowledge:0.hook: Her answer was a number that made no sense.
knowledge:0.line: '*Knowledge* of your shelves is respect for your customers.'

mental:0.en: It was a slow night. Lin sat on an upturned crate near the magazine rack and stared at nothing. I asked if she was all right. She said convenience store night shifts require more *mental* effort than people think — you are always watching, always ready, even when everything looks perfectly calm.
mental:0.cnHint: 林说便利店夜班需要很强的____专注力，看似平静其实不然。
mental:0.hook: Then the lights above the back shelf flickered once.
mental:0.line: 'The *mental* side of this job is what tires me most.'

weight:0.en: Lin came in hauling two large bags of rice, one in each hand. Tang offered to help. She shook her head. 'I know the *weight*,' she said, setting them down softly. She had clearly carried things like this many times before — but her expression said it was not just rice she meant.
weight:0.cnHint: 林独自搬着沉重的米袋，说自己知道这份____。
weight:0.hook: She stared at the floor a moment longer than necessary.
weight:0.line: 'I know the *weight* — I've been carrying it for years.'

academic:0.en: A young man came in waving a printed sheet and grinning. He had passed some *academic* contest and wanted to celebrate with canned coffee. Lin was there buying batteries. She glanced at his sheet, said nothing for a moment, then quietly told him the hardest part comes after the prize.
academic:0.cnHint: 一个赢得____竞赛的年轻人来庆祝，林的回应让他若有所思。
academic:0.hook: Lin paid and left before he could ask what she meant.
academic:0.line: 'Every *academic* win just raises the wall you face next.'

prepare:0.en: Lin arrived at 11 p.m. with a notebook full of neat lists. 'I always *prepare* before a night shift,' she said, checking the stock shelves one by one. I watched her move through the store like she already owned it. The Manager had never once mentioned a second clerk was coming tonight.
prepare:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林深夜带着笔记本来上班，她总会提前____好一切，让我感到有些意外。
prepare:0.hook: Why did the Manager forget to tell me about her?
prepare:0.line: 'I always *prepare* before a night shift — every shelf, every count.'

workplace:0.en: Tang taped a small paper sign above the kettle: KEEP TIDY, PLEASE. 'A clean *workplace* makes the whole shift easier,' he said, nodding at a ring of dried tea on the counter. He was not wrong. By morning I had wiped the counter four times, and each time I thought of that sign.
workplace:0.cnHint: 阿糖在茶壶上方贴了一张纸条，说整洁的____会让整个班次更顺畅。
workplace:0.hook: Later I found a second sign hidden behind the rice-cooker.
workplace:0.line: 'A clean *workplace* makes every shift easier — trust me on that.'

post:0.en: The Manager walked in just before midnight and *posted* a new schedule on the glass door without a word. I leaned over to read it. My name appeared three times in one week. Lin's name appeared zero. She was standing right behind me, and her face was very still.
post:0.cnHint: 店长深夜贴出了新排班表，我发现自己的名字出现了三次，而隔壁咖啡店的林的名字一次也没有____。
post:0.hook: Lin's expression told me the schedule was not news to her.
post:0.line: 'I *posted* the new schedule — check it before you clock out tonight.'

complete:0.en: 'You have to *complete* the shelf check before four a.m.,' Tang told me on my first solo night, handing over a clipboard with twelve rows. Eleven rows were easy. The twelfth row was the one behind the tall snack rack, where the light had been broken for a week.
complete:0.cnHint: 阿糖告诉我必须在凌晨四点前____货架检查，但最后一排货架的灯坏了整整一周。
complete:0.hook: Something at the back of that dark shelf made a soft rustling sound.
complete:0.line: 'You must *complete* the shelf check before four — no shortcuts.'

measure:0.en: Lin pulled a small ruler from her apron and began to *measure* the gap between the drinks cooler and the wall. 'Twelve centimetres,' she said quietly, writing it down. I had no idea why that mattered. Three days later, a brand-new display stand appeared in that exact space.
measure:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林用尺子____了饮料柜和墙壁之间的距离，三天后那个位置出现了一个新展架。
measure:0.hook: No one told me who had ordered the stand.
measure:0.line: 'Let me *measure* that gap — I have a feeling it is exactly right.'

recommend:0.en: A sleepy student shuffled in at two a.m., staring at the hot-food shelf. 'What do you *recommend*?' he asked me. I had only started four days ago, so I pointed at whatever Tang had told me was fresh. The student came back the next night and asked for exactly the same thing.
recommend:0.cnHint: 一名困倦的学生深夜进店，问我____什么，我只好指向阿糖告诉我最新鲜的那样东西。
recommend:0.hook: He returned every night that week, each time asking the same question.
recommend:0.line: 'What do you *recommend* tonight — I trust your judgment by now.'

resource:0.en: The store's back room was small, but Tang had turned it into something impressive. Every roll of tape, every spare price tag, every cleaning cloth had its place. 'This room is our best *resource*,' he said proudly. Lin appeared in the doorway, looked around once, and said nothing.
resource:0.cnHint: 阿糖把储藏室整理得井井有条，骄傲地说这里是我们最好的____，而隔壁咖啡店的林看了一眼后什么也没说。
resource:0.hook: The next evening, the cleaning cloths had been moved to a different shelf.
resource:0.line: 'This back room is our best *resource* — use it well and it will save you.'

specific:0.en: The Manager left me a note before his day off: 'Follow the closing steps.' No *specific* order was written down. I asked Tang, who listed six steps without pausing. I asked Lin, who listed eight steps in a different order. They both looked at me as if the answer were obvious.
specific:0.cnHint: 店长的便条没有写____的步骤顺序，我问阿糖和隔壁咖啡店的林，两人给出了完全不同的答案。
specific:0.hook: Somewhere between their two lists, the real answer was hiding.
specific:0.line: 'Could you give me *specific* steps — not just a wave at the shelves?'

major:0.en: The Manager calls me over before my shift starts. 'There is one *major* rule here,' he says, pointing at the coffee machine. 'Never let it run dry.' He looks at it the way people look at a sleeping cat — with great respect and a little fear. I nod seriously. I have no idea how it works.
major:0.cnHint: 店长告诉新来的我，店里有一条____规定，一定不能违反。
major:0.hook: By midnight, the machine starts making a sound I have never heard before.
major:0.line: 'There is one *major* rule here, and the coffee machine is it.'

communication:0.en: Lin from the store across the street walks in just before two in the morning. She buys a pen, which seems odd. Then I notice she has been leaving small notes under our door all week. 'Notes are better than shouting,' she says with a smile. Slow *communication*, but it works for her.
communication:0.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林用便条纸和我们____，而不是直接进门说话。
communication:0.hook: The next note has a question on it that I do not know how to answer.
communication:0.line: 'Notes are my favourite kind of *communication* — no one interrupts you.'

market:0.en: Tang tells me the night shift is a *market* of its own kind. 'Everyone who walks in after midnight needs something they can not say clearly,' she says, refilling the hot-food case. A man comes in, stares at the shelves for five minutes, and buys only a single toothpick. Tang nods like she expected it.
market:0.cnHint: 同事阿糖说深夜的便利店就像一个特殊的____，来的人都有说不清的需求。
market:0.hook: The man comes back ten minutes later and stares at the shelves again.
market:0.line: 'The night shift is a *market* you will never fully understand, trust me.'

apply:0.en: A student rushes in waving a printed form. She asks if we sell stamps. We do not. She groans. 'I have to *apply* for a library card before eight or I lose my spot,' she says, pressing her hands to her face. Tang quietly points to the self-service printer in the corner. The student stares at it like it is magic.
apply:0.cnHint: 一位同学深夜冲进来，说她需要____图书馆的证件，急得不得了。
apply:0.hook: The printer makes a strange noise and then goes very quiet.
apply:0.line: 'I need to *apply* before eight or the whole thing falls apart.'

treat:0.en: A small child comes in holding her grandfather's hand. She studies the candy shelf for a long time, very serious. Her grandfather tells her to pick one *treat* and to choose well. She picks a bag, puts it back, picks it again. I find myself holding my breath. She nods, satisfied, and places it on the counter.
treat:0.cnHint: 一个小女孩在爷爷的陪伴下，认真地挑选她的____。
treat:0.hook: She looks up at me and asks a question I am completely unprepared for.
treat:0.line: 'You may pick one *treat*, but choose well — there is no going back.'

creative:0.en: Lin comes in again, this time with a notebook. She says she is redesigning her store window and wants to know what colours we use. 'You are surprisingly *creative* for a convenience store,' she says, looking around. I am not sure if it is a compliment. The Manager, listening from the back room, smiles at the ceiling.
creative:0.cnHint: 竞争对手隔壁咖啡店的林说我们便利店出人意料地很有____，让我一时不知如何回应。
creative:0.hook: She tears a page from her notebook and slides it across the counter to me.
creative:0.line: 'You are surprisingly *creative* for a shop that just sells instant noodles.'

perform:0.en: Just before dawn, Tang shows me how to *perform* the closing count of the register. Her fingers move fast and she never looks down. 'You will be slow at first,' she says, 'but the numbers will start to feel like yours.' I try. I am slow. The sun comes up before I finish, and she is already making fresh coffee.
perform:0.cnHint: 天亮前，同事阿糖教我如何____收银台的结算，她的动作又快又准。
perform:0.hook: She glances at my total and raises one eyebrow without saying a word.
perform:0.line: 'Watch me *perform* the count once, then you try it yourself.'

career:0.en: Lin walked in just before midnight, dropping a thick folder on the counter. 'Look at this,' she said. Her old company had shut down, and now every plan for her *career* lay scattered across my register like fallen leaves. She stared at the ceiling, saying nothing.
career:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林把关于自己____的文件摊在收银台上，沉默地望着天花板。
career:0.hook: The folder held one page she clearly did not want me to see.
career:0.line: 'My *career* was supposed to start this year, not end.'

medium:0.en: The Manager keeps a small radio behind the shelf of instant noodles. He calls it his favourite *medium* for news because, he says, the voice feels warmer than any screen. Tonight Lin stood beside it, ear tilted, listening to a report about job markets with a very tight expression.
medium:0.cnHint: 店长把收音机当作获取新闻的____，隔壁咖啡店的林紧绷着脸在旁边听着。
medium:0.hook: Whatever the radio just announced made Lin set down her coffee very slowly.
medium:0.line: 'A radio is still the best *medium* when you need calm news.'

office:0.en: Lin pulled out her phone and showed me a photo: a bright, glass-walled *office* on the twentieth floor where she used to work. 'Gone,' she said simply. The building was still there in the picture, but the company name on the door had already been painted over in plain white.
office:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林给我看了她曾经工作的____的照片，门上的公司名字已经被涂白了。
office:0.hook: She zoomed in on one desk, and her hand trembled slightly.
office:0.line: 'That *office* was my whole world for three years.'

culture:0.en: Tang arrived for the early shift and found Lin still at the corner table with her folder. They began talking about work life, and Tang said every company has its own *culture*, like a secret language you only learn after months inside. Lin laughed for the first time that night.
culture:0.cnHint: 阿糖说每家公司都有自己的____，就像一种只有待久了才懂的秘密语言，这让隔壁咖啡店的林笑了。
culture:0.hook: Then Tang mentioned one company name, and Lin's smile vanished instantly.
culture:0.line: 'A good *culture* at work matters more than the salary.'

college:0.en: I asked Lin where she had studied. She pointed vaguely east and said her *college* was a small one, not famous, but the professors actually remembered your name. She said that was the last time she felt completely sure of where she belonged. I did not know what to say to that.
college:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林说她的____虽然不出名，却是她最后一次感到自己真正有归属感的地方。
college:0.hook: She then asked if I had ever felt the same way, and waited.
college:0.line: 'My *college* was small, but it felt like home.'

value:0.en: Lin picked up a chocolate bar, turned it over, and put it back. 'Too expensive,' she said. Then she stared at the shelf and added that she used to never check prices, back when she had a steady job. Knowing your own *value* at work, she said quietly, keeps you from feeling small everywhere else.
value:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林说，清楚自己在工作中的____，才能在其他地方不感到渺小。
value:0.hook: She bought the chocolate anyway and did not explain why.
value:0.line: 'You lose your job and suddenly you question your own *value*.'

connection:0.en: Lin borrowed the store phone because her battery had died. She dialled twice and got no answer. 'Old colleague,' she said with a small shrug. 'We had a good *connection* once.' She left a short message, voice steady, then handed the phone back and straightened her coat like nothing had happened.
connection:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林借店里的电话联系一位曾与她关系很好的老同事，却没人接听。
connection:0.hook: The phone buzzed with a reply just as she reached the door.
connection:0.line: 'We had a strong *connection*, but work changes people.'

story:0.en: Near dawn, Lin finally closed her folder. 'Every person in there is a whole *story*,' she said, meaning her former colleagues, each one now looking for work like her. She bought a warm can of corn soup, nodded goodnight, and walked out into the pale blue morning without looking back.
story:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林说文件夹里每个人都有一段____，然后买了罐玉米汤，走进了清晨。
story:0.hook: She left one page behind, and it had my name on it.
story:0.line: 'Everyone here has a *story* they have not told yet.'

positive:1.en: Lin stood outside the store at dawn, checking a handwritten sign in the window. She turned to me with a wide smile. 'Your sales numbers look bad,' she said, 'but I stay *positive* — my new snack display will beat yours by Friday.' The cold morning air felt suddenly competitive.
positive:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在店外看着橱窗里的告示，态度____地说她的新零食展台会赢过我们。
positive:1.hook: But she was staring at my register total, not hers.
positive:1.line: 'I stay *positive* — my display will beat yours by Friday.'

economic:1.en: The Manager stopped me near the rubbish bins behind the store. He spread a rough chart on a cardboard box. 'Look,' he said, pointing at falling lines, 'the *economic* pressure on this block is real — three shops closed last year.' He folded the chart and walked back inside without another word.
economic:1.cnHint: 店长在店外向我展示街区的____压力，已有三家店关门了。
economic:1.hook: He had underlined one number twice, and it matched our rent.
economic:1.line: 'The *economic* pressure on this block is very real, trust me.'

link:1.en: Tang and I were pulling the morning delivery inside when Lin crossed the street with a crate of her own goods. She smiled and said, 'Every store on this corner is a *link* in the same chain — if one looks bad, we all lose customers.' Then she stacked her crate neatly and walked away.
link:1.cnHint: 送货时隔壁咖啡店的林走过来说，街角每家店都是同一条链条上的____。
link:1.hook: Her crate had our store's old price tag still on it.
link:1.line: 'Every store here is a *link* — if one fails, we all suffer.'

produce:1.en: Lin had set up a small folding table on the pavement outside her store. She handed out tiny cups of a new drink. 'We *produce* this ourselves,' she told the small crowd, 'no middleman, no extra cost.' I watched from the doorway, counting how many people took a cup and smiled.
produce:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在人行道上摆摊，告诉顾客她们自己____这种新饮料。
produce:1.hook: The last person in the crowd was the Manager.
produce:1.line: 'We *produce* this drink ourselves — fresh, cheap, and only here.'

teach:1.en: Early morning, before the street got busy, Lin sat on the kerb next to me during my break. She was patient, drawing tiny diagrams in a notebook. 'Let me *teach* you how I arrange the shelves by colour,' she said quietly. 'People buy more when things look pretty.' I borrowed her pen.
teach:1.cnHint: 休息时隔壁咖啡店的林坐在路边，主动要____我她的货架陈列技巧。
teach:1.hook: She had left one page blank, as if saving it for later.
teach:1.line: 'Let me *teach* you my shelf trick — colour matters more than price.'

worth:1.en: I almost tripped on a coin outside the entrance. Lin was already crouching, picking it up. 'Not *worth* much alone,' she said, holding it to the early light, 'but the Manager counts every single one at closing.' She pressed it into my palm and nodded toward the door. I went back to work.
worth:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林捡起一枚硬币，说单独一枚不太____钱，但店长每晚都数。
worth:1.hook: The coin was warm, as if someone had dropped it on purpose.
worth:1.line: 'It is not *worth* much alone, but the Manager counts every coin.'

common:1.en: Lin leaned on the lamp post outside, watching the early bus stop across the road. 'You know what is *common* to every store that survives here?' she asked, not looking at me. 'They all know their regulars by name.' She pushed off the post and went inside without explaining why she had told me.
common:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林靠着路灯说，这里所有存活下来的店有一个____点。
common:1.hook: She already knew my regulars' names better than I did.
common:1.line: 'It is *common* to every store that lasts — know your regulars.'

daily:1.en: The street sweeper passed at six every morning, and Lin was always already outside, wiping her sign. 'This is my *daily* routine,' she told me one cold Tuesday, wringing out her cloth, 'same time, same steps, every single day.' She said it the way someone talks about a secret they do not mind sharing.
daily:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林每天擦店招牌，她把这个____习惯当作自己的小秘诀来分享。
daily:1.hook: She had been doing it for two years longer than the Manager.
daily:1.line: 'This is my *daily* routine — same time, same steps, every day.'

determine:1.en: Lin stood outside the store at midnight, studying the price list taped to the window. She was trying to *determine* whether our drinks were cheaper than her own shop across the street. She counted numbers on her fingers twice, her breath making small clouds in the cold air.
determine:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在店外仔细研究价格表，想____我们的饮料是否比她的店便宜。
determine:1.hook: Her eyes narrowed at one price in particular.
determine:1.line: 'I need to *determine* which of us has the better deal.'

response:1.en: A delivery man knocked hard on the store's glass door at two in the morning. I looked at Lin, who was passing by with her dog. She gave no *response* to his loud knocking — just raised one eyebrow at me, as if to say that was my problem now, and kept walking.
response:1.cnHint: 送货员大力敲门，隔壁咖啡店的林路过时对此毫无____，只是挑了挑眉走开了。
response:1.hook: The delivery man knocked a second time, even louder.
response:1.line: 'No *response* from inside? That is odd for this hour.'

search:1.en: Lin paced the wet pavement outside, phone raised high, turning in slow circles. I stepped out to ask if she needed help. She explained she was in *search* of a strong enough signal to send one very important message. The nearest lamp post flickered above her.
search:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在店外举着手机转圈，正在____足够强的信号。
search:1.hook: Her phone buzzed — but it was not the reply she wanted.
search:1.line: 'I am in *search* of a signal, not your company.'

regard:1.en: The street sweeper stopped his cart to talk with Lin outside our window each morning. He clearly *regarded* her as one of the most important people on the block. I watched them laugh together and wondered what she had done to earn such warmth from everyone except us.
regard:1.cnHint: 扫街大爷显然非常____隔壁咖啡店的林，每天都会停下来和她聊天。
regard:1.hook: That morning, the sweeper glanced toward our store with a strange look.
regard:1.line: 'Everyone on this street *regards* her as a good neighbor.'

true:1.en: I overheard Lin telling a woman outside that our store sold expired snacks. I was ready to argue, but the Manager touched my arm. He said the *true* answer was better than anger. He walked out, smiled, and invited the woman in to check every date herself.
true:1.cnHint: Manager说，用____来回应比争吵更有力，邀请顾客亲自检查日期。
true:1.hook: The woman stepped inside, and Lin watched in silence.
true:1.line: 'The *true* way to win is to simply show the facts.'

depend:1.en: Tang and I debated whether Lin would cut her prices again this week. Tang said it would *depend* on how many customers she had seen coming to us lately. We both turned to look out the window. Lin was already outside, counting people who walked through our door.
depend:1.cnHint: 阿糖说隔壁咖啡店的林是否降价要____她观察到多少顾客来我们店。
depend:1.hook: Lin pulled out a small notebook and began to write.
depend:1.line: 'It will all *depend* on what I see this week.'

expensive:1.en: Lin held up a bottle of juice from our outdoor rack and shook her head slowly at the price tag. 'Too *expensive*,' she said to no one, loudly enough for passing shoppers to hear. She set it back carefully, smiled at one curious customer, and walked back to her own shop.
expensive:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林大声说我们的果汁太____了，刚好让路过的顾客都能听见。
expensive:1.hook: Two shoppers stopped walking and looked at our price tag.
expensive:1.line: 'This is far too *expensive* — my shop sells it cheaper.'

explain:1.en: Lin stops me just outside the store, under the yellow streetlight. She points at the sign above our door, then at the identical sign above the shop across the road. 'You should *explain* to the Manager why our prices need to change,' she says, voice low. 'Before he finds out from someone else.'
explain:1.cnHint: 林在店门口拦住我，要我向店长____价格的问题。
explain:1.hook: The other shop's sign flickers — someone is standing behind it.
explain:1.line: 'You need to *explain* this to the Manager before tomorrow morning.'

examine:1.en: A delivery box sits on the pavement outside the store entrance. Lin crouches beside it, brow tight. She lifts each item and turns it slowly. 'I always *examine* every order before it goes inside,' she tells me. 'Last month a whole crate of drinks was already bad when it arrived.'
examine:1.cnHint: 林在店门口仔细____每一件到货商品。
examine:1.hook: At the very bottom of the box, something is wrapped in plain paper.
examine:1.line: 'I *examine* every box. You should do the same on your shift.'

influence:1.en: We are both standing on the corner, watching people walk past the rival store across the street. Lin crosses her arms. 'A clean window and a good light can *influence* where people choose to stop,' she says quietly. 'That place knows it. That is why they repainted last week.'
influence:1.cnHint: 林说，店面的外观会____顾客选择进哪家店。
influence:1.hook: A woman slows down in front of the rival store, then glances our way.
influence:1.line: 'Small details *influence* customers more than you might think.'

argue:1.en: Tang and Lin are on the pavement just outside the door, voices rising above the sound of passing bicycles. I step out to listen. They *argue* about who forgot to put up the weekly sale board. Neither will back down. A regular customer squeezes between them with a polite cough.
argue:1.cnHint: 唐和林在店门口为谁忘了摆促销牌而____。
argue:1.hook: The regular customer stops, turns around, and holds up a crumpled notice.
argue:1.line: 'There is no point to *argue* here — the board is simply gone.'

pass:1.en: I am restocking the shelf by the window when a familiar figure *passes* by on the street outside. It is Lin, walking fast, a stack of flyers under her arm and a determined look on her face. She does not glance at our store. She is heading straight for the block of offices nearby.
pass:1.cnHint: 我看见林拿着传单从店外____，径直走向附近的办公楼。
pass:1.hook: Every flyer in that stack has our store's corner printed on the front.
pass:1.line: 'I always *pass* this corner at six — it tells me how busy the night will be.'

serious:1.en: Lin catches me sweeping the pavement and stops. Her voice is calm but her eyes are not. 'The Manager is *serious* about closing the night shift if numbers do not improve this month,' she says. A cat sits on the wall beside us, perfectly still, as if it too is waiting for my answer.
serious:1.cnHint: 林告诉我，如果本月业绩不好，店长____考虑关掉夜班。
serious:1.hook: The cat jumps down and walks slowly toward the rival store across the road.
serious:1.line: 'I am *serious* — the Manager has already done the numbers twice.'

despite:1.en: Rain starts just as Lin finishes taping a new poster to the outside wall. She steps back and looks at it with quiet pride. *Despite* the wet, she does not move inside. 'A poster seen in the rain is remembered,' she says, pulling her jacket tighter. I hand her an umbrella.
despite:1.cnHint: 林____下雨，坚持把海报贴在店外的墙上。
despite:1.hook: The poster shows a price that is lower than anything we currently sell.
despite:1.line: 'I finished it *despite* the rain, and I would do it again.'

express:1.en: Lin is leaning against the lamppost outside when I arrive for my shift. She looks at me for a moment, then at the quiet street. 'I want to *express* something to the Manager,' she says carefully, 'but I am not sure he is ready to hear it yet.' She pushes off the post and walks inside ahead of me.
express:1.cnHint: 林说她想向店长____某件事，但还不确定时机是否成熟。
express:1.hook: She pauses at the door, as if deciding whether to turn back.
express:1.line: 'I will *express* my idea tonight — if the moment feels right.'

trouble:0.en: Lin walked in at midnight carrying a mop and a frown. She worked at the store across the street and had come to borrow our cleaning supplies — again. 'No *trouble*,' she said, flashing a quick smile, but I noticed she stayed to chat for twenty minutes.
trouble:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林深夜来借清洁用品，说不会造成____，却聊了很久才走。
trouble:0.hook: She glanced back once at the door — like she was checking something.
trouble:0.line: 'No *trouble* at all — I just need the mop for ten minutes.'

reflect:0.en: The front window was spotless after my first cleaning shift. In the quiet hour before dawn, I could see the whole store *reflected* in it — the soft lights, the neat rows of snacks, and Lin across the street, watching. I waved. She didn't wave back.
reflect:0.cnHint: 夜深人静时，整洁的橱窗____出店内的样子，以及对街盯着这边的隔壁咖啡店的林。
reflect:0.hook: Her lights clicked off a second later — all of them, at once.
