reflect:0.line: 'The glass *reflects* everything — even things people don't mean to show.'

attend:0.en: Tang told me the Manager used to *attend* every neighborhood meeting on this block, back when the store first opened. 'He knew every face,' Tang said, stacking juice boxes neatly. Lin came in just then, bought one bottle of water, and left without a word.
attend:0.cnHint: 阿糖说店长以前会____街区会议，认识每一张面孔，而隔壁咖啡店的林只买了一瓶水就沉默离开。
attend:0.hook: Tang watched the door close and murmured something too quiet to catch.
attend:0.line: 'He used to *attend* every meeting — he never missed one, not once.'

belief:0.en: Lin stopped by just before three in the morning, arms crossed. 'My *belief* is that a good store earns loyalty slowly,' she said, eyeing our snack display with a sharp look. The Manager, who had been quietly restocking behind me, simply smiled and said nothing.
belief:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在深夜表达了她对好店铺的____，店长只是微笑，没有接话。
belief:0.hook: She bought nothing, but she stood there for a full minute before leaving.
belief:0.line: 'My *belief* is that price is not what keeps people coming back.'

carry:0.en: Lin arrived with a box so large I could barely see her face above it. 'Just passing by,' she said, which was hard to believe since she clearly needed two hands to *carry* the thing. Tang raised an eyebrow. The box had our store's name printed on the side.
carry:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林抱着一个大箱子说只是路过，但那箱子需要双手____，而且印着我们店的名字。
carry:0.hook: She set it down on our counter and didn't explain.
carry:0.line: 'I can *carry* it myself — I don't need any help, thank you.'

else:0.en: Lin leaned on the counter at 2 a.m. and looked around slowly. 'You should move the drinks,' she said. 'And maybe *else* — the whole far shelf.' I blinked. No one had asked for her advice. The Manager appeared from the back and nodded, as if he had heard everything.
else:0.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林深夜主动建议调整货架摆放，还说应该改动____的地方，店长从后面走出来若有所思地点头。
else:0.hook: He looked at Lin with an expression I had never seen on his face before.
else:0.line: 'Move the drinks, and everything *else* on that shelf, to the left wall.'

policy:1.en: Lin stopped outside our door and pointed at the sign I had just taped to the glass. 'No returns after midnight,' it read. She crossed her arms and asked where the rule came from. I explained that the Manager had written a clear *policy* about it last week. Lin studied the sign for a long moment, then pulled out a notebook and began writing something down.
policy:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在门外看到新规定的告示，询问这条____从哪里来，然后默默记录下来。
policy:1.hook: Whatever she wrote in that notebook, I had a feeling it was not a shopping list.
policy:1.line: 'Show me where this *policy* is written, and I will decide if it is fair.'

industry:1.en: Lin leaned against the lamp post outside, chatting with the Manager about her work. She said the food delivery *industry* had changed everything on this street — half the shops closed by nine, yet our little store was still bright at two in the morning. The Manager smiled and said nothing. I pretended to stack cups and listened as hard as I could.
industry:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在店外和店长聊起，送餐____改变了整条街的生意格局。
industry:1.hook: The Manager's smile faded the moment Lin turned to look at the empty shop next door.
industry:1.line: 'The delivery *industry* is eating every small shop alive — except yours, somehow.'

concern:1.en: I was sweeping the step outside when Lin walked over, hands in pockets. She said it with a calm voice: her only *concern* was that our late-night noodle special was pulling customers away from her own store two doors down. I nodded, unsure what to say. She gave a small shrug, bought a bottle of water, and left without another word.
concern:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林平静地告诉我，她唯一的____是我们的夜宵特惠抢走了她的客人。
concern:1.hook: She had been that calm once before, Tang later told me — right before she redesigned her whole menu overnight.
concern:1.line: 'My only *concern* is that your prices are just a little too good at midnight.'

present:1.en: Outside, under the yellow street light, a small boy handed his grandfather a bag from our store. The grandfather opened it slowly: one warm meat bun and a pair of cheap reading glasses. The boy beamed. 'I bought it with my own money,' he said proudly. It was a modest *present*, but the old man's eyes went bright. I watched from the doorway and felt unexpectedly warm.
present:1.cnHint: 小男孩在街灯下把从我们店买的____交给爷爷，那是他用零花钱买的。
present:1.hook: The grandfather tucked the glasses into his pocket and whispered something I could not hear from the doorway.
present:1.line: 'It is just a small *present*, Grandpa, but I picked it out myself.'

claim:1.en: Lin stood at the kerb outside and pointed at our handwritten chalk board. She said she had the same lunch-box deal last year and that we had simply copied her idea. I had no answer ready. Tang, who was passing by on the way in, stopped and told her she was welcome to *claim* credit — but our box had three more side dishes. Lin stared at the board, then at Tang, then walked away.
claim:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林声称我们抄了她的便当套餐创意，阿糖则指出我们的套餐多了三道配菜。
claim:1.hook: Lin glanced back once before she turned the corner, and that one look told me this was far from over.
claim:1.line: 'You can *claim* it was your idea, but our customers seem to prefer ours.'

half:1.en: It was nearly three in the morning. Lin was sitting on the low wall outside our store, eating a rice ball she had bought from us — not from her own place. She looked a little tired. I brought her a small cup of hot tea without being asked. She accepted it, drank *half*, and set the rest on the wall beside her without comment. The street was completely quiet.
half:1.cnHint: 凌晨三点，隔壁咖啡店的林坐在店外吃着从我们这买的饭团，喝了____杯我递给她的热茶后没有说话。
half:1.hook: She sat there for ten more minutes, and I began to wonder what kept her out this late every night.
half:1.line: 'I only drank *half* — I am not sure yet if I like accepting help from a rival.'

successful:1.en: The Manager was locking the side door when Lin stopped him on the pavement. She asked, straight out, how a tiny store like ours managed to stay *successful* when every other shop on the block was struggling. The Manager looked up at the sky as if thinking hard, then said, 'We remember people's names.' Lin was quiet for a moment. Then she asked, 'What is mine?'
successful:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在路上拦住店长，问这家小店为何能保持____，店长的回答出乎她意料。
successful:1.hook: The Manager smiled and said her name perfectly, and Lin's expression shifted in a way I had never seen before.
successful:1.line: 'Tell me honestly — what made you *successful* when the rest of us are barely keeping up?'

access:1.en: Lin was standing outside, trying to log into the store's free street Wi-Fi. She kept getting an error. I stepped out and typed the new code for her without thinking twice. She looked surprised. 'You are giving me *access*?' she said. I shrugged and told her the signal reached her shop anyway — she might as well use it properly. She laughed, once, quietly, and it was the first real laugh I had heard from her.
access:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在门外连不上免费Wi-Fi，我帮她输入新密码，给了她____，她的反应让我意外。
access:1.hook: As she walked back to her own store, she paused and looked at our sign, and I thought I saw her smile again.
access:1.line: 'You are really giving me *access* to your Wi-Fi — just like that, no conditions?'

conduct:1.en: Lin stood outside our store at midnight, watching how I handled the late rush. I did not know then that she ran the shop across the street. My *conduct* behind the counter — calm, quick, never rude — seemed to interest her more than the products on our shelves.
conduct:1.cnHint: 林站在店外，仔细观察我的____，神情若有所思。
conduct:1.hook: Why was she writing notes in a small black book?
conduct:1.line: 'Your *conduct* tonight was better than I expected from a new clerk.'

reveal:1.en: Lin pushed open our door just before dawn and walked straight to the drinks fridge. She grabbed two cold teas, set one on the counter for me, and smiled. That one small act began to *reveal* a side of her the Manager had never mentioned — generous, almost warm.
reveal:1.cnHint: 林的一个小举动开始____出她不为人知的一面。
reveal:1.hook: She left before I could even say thank you.
reveal:1.line: 'I did not mean to *reveal* anything — I just thought you looked tired.'

powerful:1.en: A cold wind swept the street corner just after two in the morning. Lin walked past our window without stopping, her coat pulled tight. Even then she looked *powerful* — chin up, steps steady, as if the wind were something she had already beaten before.
powerful:1.cnHint: 深夜寒风中，林走过街角，步伐显得格外____。
powerful:1.hook: She paused at the corner and looked back once.
powerful:1.line: 'You have to look *powerful* out there, or the street will eat you alive.'

push:1.en: Lin taped a new sign in her shop window just after sunrise: ten percent off everything. I watched from our door. The Manager sighed and said it was her usual morning *push* to pull customers away before the breakfast crowd reached us. The game was already on.
push:1.cnHint: 林一早就开始了她的促销____，试图在早高峰前抢走顾客。
push:1.hook: The Manager's eye twitched in a way I had never seen before.
push:1.line: 'Every morning *push* she makes, we answer with better service — remember that.'

wonder:1.en: At three in the morning the street was empty except for Lin, who sat on the low wall outside her shop and looked up at the sky. I felt a quiet *wonder* watching her — this sharp rival of ours, suddenly small and still under all those stars.
wonder:1.cnHint: 凌晨三点，我望着独自仰望星空的林，心中涌起一种____。
wonder:1.hook: She mouthed something to the sky I could not read.
wonder:1.line: 'Don't you ever *wonder* why we both chose a corner like this one?'

design:1.en: Lin came in at noon to buy a pen. While I found change she studied our new shelf layout — the one Tang had stayed late to arrange. She said nothing, but I could tell she was already starting to *design* something similar for her own side of the street.
design:1.cnHint: 林悄悄打量着我们新布置的货架，心里似乎在____她自己的方案。
design:1.hook: She bought two extra pens she clearly did not need.
design:1.line: 'I like to *design* my shelves myself — no one else gets the logic right.'

exercise:1.en: Every morning at six, Lin jogged past our window twice before opening her shop. Tang called it her warm-up. The Manager called it a show. I just thought it was nice to *exercise* before a long day of standing — I had started doing the same thing on my breaks.
exercise:1.cnHint: 林每天早晨都会在开店前____，这让店长和唐各有看法。
exercise:1.hook: One morning she slowed down and glanced at me through the glass.
exercise:1.line: 'If you don't *exercise* before a twelve-hour shift, your legs will hate you by midnight.'

space:1.en: Lin's shop was half the size of ours, but she used every corner well. When I passed by on my lunch break I noticed she had left one small *space* near the door completely empty — just a stool and a lamp. It felt intentional, like a quiet place she had kept for herself.
space:1.cnHint: 林把店里一处小____留得空空荡荡，只有一把凳子和一盏灯。
space:1.hook: The stool had a single dried flower on it that I had not noticed before.
space:1.line: 'A little *space* with nothing in it can make the whole room feel bigger — try it.'

career:1.en: Outside the store, Lin stood under a lamp post, staring at a business card. 'I almost took that job,' she said quietly. Her whole *career* had led her here, to this corner, on this cold night. She looked up and noticed me watching through the glass.
career:1.cnHint: 林站在路灯下，盯着一张名片，思考自己的____。
career:1.hook: She slipped the card into her pocket and walked straight inside.
career:1.line: 'My *career* took a strange turn — and I ended up here.'

medium:1.en: A street artist was drawing portraits near the crosswalk. Lin stopped to watch. 'Paper is not the right *medium* for night work,' he said, holding up a smudged sheet. She laughed, and I heard it clearly through the open store door.
medium:1.cnHint: 一位街头画家向林解释，纸张不是夜晚创作的合适____。
medium:1.hook: Then the artist turned his sketchbook toward Lin, and her smile faded.
medium:1.line: 'Paper is not the right *medium* for what I want to express.'

office:1.en: Lin arrived early, before her shift, carrying a box of files. 'I just cleared out my old *office*,' she told me, setting the box on the bench outside. She paused at the door, looking back at the box as if saying goodbye to something.
office:1.cnHint: 林带着一箱文件来到店门口，说自己刚清理了旧____。
office:1.hook: She never explained why she had left, and I was afraid to ask.
office:1.line: 'I cleared out my *office* today — lighter now, mostly.'

culture:1.en: Two students sat on the kerb outside, debating loudly. Lin passed them and stopped. 'That is the real *culture* of this street,' she said with a grin, pointing at their half-eaten noodle cups and open notebooks. I stepped out to listen, curious.
culture:1.cnHint: 林指着街边的学生和泡面碗，笑称这才是这条街的真正____。
culture:1.hook: One student looked up and asked Lin a question she clearly did not expect.
culture:1.line: 'Half-eaten noodles and open books — that is *culture* to me.'

college:1.en: Lin was leaning on the wall outside, reading a flyer about a night class. 'I never finished *college*,' she said without looking up, her voice flat and steady. A bus rolled past, its lights sweeping across her face for just a moment.
college:1.cnHint: 林盯着夜校传单，平静地说自己没读完____。
college:1.hook: She folded the flyer slowly and tucked it under her arm.
college:1.line: 'I never finished *college*, but I never stopped studying either.'

value:1.en: A man offered Lin a coin he found on the pavement. 'No real *value*,' he said, laughing. Lin took it anyway, turned it over carefully, and held it up to the street light. 'Things keep their value longer than people think,' she told him.
value:1.cnHint: 一个陌生人把地上的硬币给了林，说它没什么____，但林不这么认为。
value:1.hook: She was still holding the coin when she walked into the store.
value:1.line: 'Things keep their *value* longer than most people believe.'

connection:1.en: Lin was fixing a loose wire on the outdoor sign when I came out to sweep. 'No *connection*, no light,' she muttered, touching two wires together until the sign buzzed back on. She looked pleased, the way someone does when a small thing goes right.
connection:1.cnHint: 林在店外修路牌线路，说没有____就没有灯光。
connection:1.hook: The sign flickered once more, and then went dark again completely.

story:1.en: Lin sat on the step outside, writing in a small notebook. 'Every regular has a *story*,' she said, without looking up. 'That man with the umbrella, the woman who only buys milk — all of them.' She closed the notebook before I could read a word.
story:1.cnHint: 林坐在台阶上写小本子，说每个常客都有一段____。
story:1.hook: Then she glanced up and added, 'So do you.'

sign:1.en: I stepped outside to drag in the sandwich board before the rain started. That's when I noticed Lin across the street, staring at our store's *sign* — the bright yellow one the Manager had just put up last week — with an expression I couldn't quite read.
sign:1.cnHint: 我把店外的广告牌搬进来时，发现林正盯着我们店的____看。
sign:1.hook: She pulled out a notebook and started writing something down.

feeling:1.en: The night air outside smelled of wet pavement and noodles from the cart down the road. I had a strange *feeling* that I was being watched, and when I turned around, Lin was leaning against the lamppost across the street, arms folded, studying our store window with calm, steady eyes.
feeling:1.cnHint: 站在店外，我有一种奇怪的____，觉得有人在观察我。
feeling:1.hook: She gave me a slow nod before walking away into the dark.
feeling:1.line: 'I have a *feeling* your Manager is planning something big.'

professional:1.en: Lin walked past our door just as I was wiping down the outside display shelf. She was dressed sharply, carrying a clipboard, looking every bit the *professional* — far more put-together than me in my wrinkled uniform and half-tied apron. She didn't even glance at me.
professional:1.cnHint: 林走过我们门口时，看起来像个十足的____，让我有点自惭形秽。
professional:1.hook: But she paused, one step past me, and tilted her head.
professional:1.line: 'A *professional* always checks the competition in person.'

behind:1.en: I was restocking the small outdoor magazine rack when I realised Lin's store had a brand-new awning and a fresh coat of paint. Our place, by contrast, looked a little worn. We were clearly *behind* in the 'looking good from the street' competition — not that the Manager would ever admit it.
behind:1.cnHint: 我发现我们店在外观上____林家的店，这让我有些担心。
behind:1.hook: Then the Manager came out and saw it too.
behind:1.line: 'We are not *behind* — we are saving money on style.'

government:1.en: A small notice was taped to the lamppost outside our store. I leaned in to read it: a *government* health inspection was scheduled for all food-service businesses on our street next Tuesday. Lin, walking past at that exact moment, had clearly already read it — she was smiling.
government:1.cnHint: 路灯柱上贴了一张____通知，林看到后面带微笑地走开了。
government:1.hook: I suddenly remembered the shelf in our back room.
government:1.line: 'The *government* notice says Tuesday — you should get ready.'

growth:1.en: Lin paused on the pavement, looking at the small potted plant the Manager had placed by our entrance. It was a little sad-looking, to be honest. She compared it to the tall, leafy tree outside her own store and said something about *growth* that I didn't fully catch, though her tone said everything.
growth:1.cnHint: 林看了看我们门口那盆小植物，说了句关于____的话，语气意味深长。
growth:1.hook: I went inside and quietly watered our poor little plant.
growth:1.line: 'Real *growth* takes time, but you should start soon.'

negative:1.en: Tang and I were standing outside on a short break when Lin walked by and glanced at our customer-count board — we track hourly visits with magnets. The number was low. She said nothing, but her look was anything but *negative*; it was almost kind, which somehow felt worse than criticism.
negative:1.cnHint: 林路过时看了眼我们的客流记录，表情并不____，却让我更难受。
negative:1.hook: Tang crushed his paper cup and headed back inside.
negative:1.line: 'Don't be *negative* — slow nights teach you things.'

potential:1.en: Lin stopped in front of our store, tilted her head, and looked at the corner spot we occupied — the crossroads, the bus stop nearby, the steady foot traffic. 'Good corner,' she said quietly. I realised she wasn't threatening us; she was acknowledging *potential* she clearly wished her own store had.
potential:1.cnHint: 林打量着我们店所在的街角，若有所思地评价了一下这里的____。
potential:1.hook: She walked away, but her eyes stayed on the corner a beat too long.
potential:1.line: 'This spot has real *potential* — someone smart chose it.'

real:1.en: It was past midnight when Lin stopped outside the store window, staring in. I watched her from behind the counter. She was checking our prices against a small notebook. The gap between her shop and ours was *real* — our shelves were fuller, our lights brighter, our line of customers longer.
real:1.cnHint: 林站在店外，悄悄比较两家店的差距，这个差距是____的。
real:1.hook: She wrote one last number, then smiled — and that smile worried me.
real:1.line: 'The difference is *real*, and I am going to fix it.'

talk:1.en: Lin caught me taking out the recycling at two in the morning. She leaned against the wall, arms crossed, and started to make small *talk* about the weather. But her eyes kept drifting to the crates of fresh drinks stacked by our back door. Nobody discusses weather at two in the morning for fun.
talk:1.cnHint: 林在店外和我闲聊，但她的眼神一直盯着我们刚到的货物。
talk:1.hook: She asked one final question that had nothing to do with the weather.
talk:1.line: 'Nice night for a little *talk*, don't you think?'

energy:1.en: Lin jogged past the store three times before sunrise, each lap a little faster. Tang watched from the doorway, sipping hot tea. 'Look at that *energy*,' Tang said quietly. I stacked the morning bread and tried not to feel tired. Outside, Lin showed no sign of slowing down, or of leaving us alone.
energy:1.cnHint: 林在天亮前多次跑过我们店门口，同事忍不住感叹她的____。
energy:1.hook: On her fourth lap, Lin stopped and stared directly at our sign.
energy:1.line: 'You have to respect that kind of *energy*,' Tang said, shaking their head.

plan:1.en: I found a folded paper near the bus stop outside, just as my shift ended. It was a hand-drawn map of our street, with notes in neat columns. Prices. Opening hours. Delivery times. Someone had a very careful *plan* for taking our customers. The handwriting looked familiar.
plan:1.cnHint: 我在公交站旁捡到一张纸，上面写满了针对我们店的____。
plan:1.hook: The last line on the paper read: 'Start Tuesday.'
plan:1.line: 'Every good *plan* needs a starting point,' the note said at the top.

bear:1.en: A delivery driver dropped a heavy crate of bottled water right in front of our door, blocking the entrance. Lin watched from across the street, arms folded. I had to *bear* the whole weight alone to drag it inside. Tang arrived late, took one look, and handed me a cold drink without a word.
bear:1.cnHint: 一箱重货挡住了店门，我只能独自____这份重量把它搬进去。
bear:1.hook: Lin crossed the street slowly, and I had a feeling she wanted to ask something.
bear:1.line: 'Can you really *bear* all that by yourself?' Lin called over.

organization:1.en: A small van pulled up at dawn, and two people in matching jackets began handing out flyers in front of our store. The flyers were for Lin's shop. Tang read one carefully and whistled low. 'She joined some kind of *organization*,' Tang said. 'They help small shops grow.' The van drove off, leaving a pile of flyers at our door.
organization:1.cnHint: 林加入了一个帮助小店发展的____，并派人在我们店门口发传单。
organization:1.hook: The last flyer had a date circled in red: this Saturday.
organization:1.line: 'That *organization* means she is serious this time,' Tang said quietly.

opportunity:1.en: The traffic lights on our corner broke just after midnight, slowing every car to a crawl. Drivers wound down their windows, looking bored. I stepped outside with a tray of free sample drinks. Tang grinned. 'Nice *opportunity*,' Tang said. We handed out every cup in ten minutes. Across the street, Lin's shop stayed dark and closed.
opportunity:1.cnHint: 路口红绿灯坏了，我抓住这个____出门给堵车的司机派发免费试饮。
opportunity:1.hook: One driver took a cup, paused, and asked for our store's address.
opportunity:1.line: 'You should not waste an *opportunity* like this,' Tang said, still grinning.

professor:1.en: An older man in a neat coat came in just before three in the morning, buying nothing but a small notebook and a pen. He told me he was a *professor* who lived nearby and liked to write at night when the street was quiet. Lin was sitting on the bench outside, also writing. They nodded at each other like old friends.
professor:1.cnHint: 一位深夜来买文具的____和坐在门外写字的林相互点头，像是旧识。
professor:1.hook: The professor glanced back at me before turning the corner and said one strange thing.
professor:1.line: 'Even a *professor* needs a quiet street and a good pen,' he said, smiling.

force:1.en: Lin stood outside our store at midnight, arms crossed, staring at the new sign I had just put up. 'You can't *force* people to switch stores,' she said, loud enough for a passing couple to hear. I smiled and offered her a free coffee sample. She took it. She drank it slowly, saying nothing.
force:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在门外盯着新招牌，说不能用____让顾客改变选择，但她还是接受了免费咖啡。
force:1.hook: She left without a word, but she glanced back twice.
force:1.line: 'You can't *force* people to change where they shop.'

importance:1.en: The Manager taped a handwritten note to the front door before heading home: 'Remember the *importance* of a warm greeting.' I read it three times, then practised smiling at my own reflection in the dark glass. A minute later, someone actually walked in.
importance:1.cnHint: 店长在门上贴了一张纸条，提醒我微笑问候的____，我对着玻璃练习了起来。
importance:1.hook: The customer who walked in looked exactly like the Manager's old photo on the wall.
importance:1.line: 'Never forget the *importance* of making a customer feel welcome.'

sell:1.en: Tang leaned on the counter after his shift and sighed. 'A hard *sell* tonight,' he said, nodding toward a stack of unsold rice balls. 'Nobody wants cold food at two in the morning.' Then, as if on cue, a hungry student pushed open the door and eyed the whole stack.
sell:1.cnHint: 阿糖感叹今晚的____很难做，整叠饭团没人要，结果一个饥饿的学生推门进来了。
sell:1.hook: The student bought every last one and asked if we had more.
sell:1.line: 'It was a hard *sell* tonight — nobody wanted the rice balls.'

replace:1.en: I found a cracked shelf bracket near the door and tried to *replace* it before the morning rush. Tang handed me a new one without even looking up from his phone. 'Third time this month,' he said cheerfully. Outside, someone was already waiting, nose pressed to the glass.
replace:1.cnHint: 我发现货架支架裂了，正试着____它，阿糖随手递来一个新的，说这个月已经是第三次了。
replace:1.hook: The person outside had been standing there for ten minutes without moving.
replace:1.line: 'We need to *replace* that bracket before the Manager sees it.'

approach:1.en: Lin's *approach* to competing with us was unusual: she stood at the corner every evening handing out little maps showing both stores, letting customers decide. I watched from our doorway, curious. Tonight she folded the last map very carefully and put it in her pocket instead of giving it away.
approach:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林用一种不寻常的____来竞争——她给顾客两家店的地图，让他们自己选，但今晚她把最后一张收进了口袋。
approach:1.hook: That folded map had something written on the back.
approach:1.line: 'My *approach* is simple — let the customers decide for themselves.'

engage:1.en: The Manager told me my job was to *engage* with every person who walked through the door, not just scan their items and wave goodbye. I tried it on the next customer, a quiet older man buying just one can of soup. He ended up telling me about his garden for fifteen minutes.
engage:1.cnHint: 店长说我的工作是和每位顾客____，而不只是扫码收钱，结果一个买汤罐头的老人和我聊了十五分钟。
engage:1.hook: He promised to bring me a tomato from his garden tomorrow.
engage:1.line: 'You have to *engage* with the customers, not just ring them up.'

ensure:1.en: Before Lin opened her store each morning, she walked the outside of both buildings to *ensure* the pavement was clean and the signs were straight — ours included. I noticed this for the first time at six in the morning and just stood there, holding a broom I had not yet used.
ensure:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林每天早上会检查两家店门前的环境，____一切整洁，我拿着扫帚呆站在那里，什么都还没做。
ensure:1.hook: She caught me staring and said nothing, just smiled a little.
ensure:1.line: 'I *ensure* the front is clean every morning — good for everyone.'

limit:1.en: Tang showed me the staff snack shelf on my first outdoor break: three items each, no more. 'The Manager set the *limit* after I ate half a shelf one night,' he said, grinning at a distant memory. I picked my three carefully. Somewhere behind me, shoes stopped on the pavement.
limit:1.cnHint: 阿糖告诉我员工零食的____是每人三样，因为他某晚吃了半架子被店长规定的，这时身后有脚步声停了下来。
limit:1.hook: The Manager was standing right there, counting quietly under her breath.
limit:1.line: 'Three snacks per person — the Manager set that *limit* herself.'

video:1.en: A city worker stopped outside and pointed a phone at our store front. I stepped out and asked if everything was okay. He said he was making a *video* report of street lights for the city office. The lamp above our sign had been dark for a week. I had not even noticed.
video:1.cnHint: 一位城市工作人员在店外拍____，说是要记录路灯损坏的情况，我才意识到我们门口的灯已经坏了一个星期。
video:1.hook: He asked if I had seen anything strange happen under that dark lamp.
video:1.line: 'I am making a *video* of every broken light on this street,' he said.

prevent:1.en: A heavy rain started without warning. I grabbed a mop and pushed a folded towel against the bottom of the door to *prevent* water from creeping inside. Two customers were stuck under our small roof, laughing and sharing an umbrella that was far too small for both of them.
prevent:1.cnHint: 突然下起大雨，我赶紧用毛巾堵住门缝来____雨水进店，两位顾客则躲在屋檐下笑着共撑一把伞。
prevent:1.hook: One of them glanced at me through the window in a way I could not read.
prevent:1.line: 'We need to *prevent* the rain from reaching the snack shelf,' Tang said, pointing urgently.

source:1.en: The music drifting into our store at two in the morning was soft and lovely. I leaned out the door and looked up and down the quiet street. A man sat on a low wall across the road, playing a small instrument I did not know. He was the *source* of the whole gentle sound.
source:1.cnHint: 凌晨两点，悠扬的音乐飘进店里，我探出门去，发现对面矮墙上坐着一个男人——他才是这美妙声音的____。
source:1.hook: When I looked again five minutes later, the wall was empty.
source:1.line: 'Do you know the *source* of that music?' I asked Tang, who only shrugged.

available:1.en: A woman in a heavy coat knocked hard on our door at three in the morning and asked if any hot soup was *available*. I checked the small pot behind the counter that Tang always kept warm. There was just enough left. The woman held the cup with both hands and closed her eyes.
available:1.cnHint: 凌晨三点，一位穿厚外套的女士来问有没有热汤____，我发现唐留在锅里的汤刚好还够一杯。
available:1.hook: She whispered a name before she took her first sip.
available:1.line: 'Is any hot food *available* right now?' she asked, her voice very tired.

customer:1.en: The last *customer* before dawn was a tall man who bought only one small box of matches. He paid with exact coins, nodded once, and walked out into the grey morning light without a word. I watched him cross the empty street. He stopped at the corner and looked back at me.
customer:1.cnHint: 黎明前的最后一位____只买了一盒火柴，付完钱后默默走出去，走到街角时却回头看了我一眼。
customer:1.hook: He had left something small on the counter that was not a receipt.
customer:1.line: 'Every *customer* who comes at this hour has a story,' Tang said quietly to me.

language:1.en: A young man came in and tried to ask me something, but his words were a mix of several things I could not follow. I smiled and pointed at items slowly. We found a way. He left happy with a warm drink and a meat bun. Sometimes the store is its own *language*.
language:1.cnHint: 一个年轻人用我听不懂的混合____问我问题，我们最后靠手势和指认商品解决了沟通难题，他高兴地离开了。
language:1.hook: He slipped a small handwritten card into my shirt pocket on the way out.
language:1.line: 'The *language* of pointing and smiling works every time,' Tang said, laughing.

test:1.en: The Manager left me alone for the first time on a busy Friday night with a simple note: 'Good luck.' I think it was a *test*. Every shelf ran low, the card reader froze twice, and a dog somehow got inside. I handled all of it. The Manager said nothing the next morning. Just smiled.
test:1.cnHint: 店长第一次在繁忙的周五夜晚把我一个人留下，我觉得这是一次____——收银机卡了两次，还有一只狗跑进来了，但我都应付过去了。
test:1.hook: Then the Manager slid a small key across the counter to me.
test:1.line: 'Consider tonight a *test* of how well you know this store,' the Manager said.

save:1.en: Outside the store, Lin stood at the bus stop with a small notebook, watching every coin she spent. She told me she was trying to *save* enough money to open her own shop one day — a place just like this one, but better. The cold wind did not seem to bother her at all.
save:1.cnHint: 林在公交站记录每一笔花销，努力____钱实现自己的梦想。
save:1.hook: Her notebook had a name written on the cover — our store's name.
save:1.line: 'I *save* a little every week, no matter what,' Lin said quietly.

service:1.en: A city worker was fixing the streetlight just outside our door. Lin stopped to watch, arms crossed, clearly judging how long it was taking. She turned to me and said the *service* in this neighbourhood had been slow for years. I wrote that down, not sure why it felt important.
service:1.cnHint: 林在店外批评街道的____效率太低，让我觉得她心里有什么计划。
service:1.hook: She pulled out her phone and took three careful photos of the broken light.
service:1.line: 'The *service* around here is slow — someone should do something,' Lin said.

note:1.en: Lin was sitting on the front step of the building next door, writing fast in a small book. I brought her a warm drink from inside. She looked up, smiled, and closed the book quickly. I had only managed to catch one word from her *note* before the cover snapped shut: 'tonight.'
note:1.cnHint: 林坐在店门外飞快地写____，我只瞥到了一个字就被她合上了。
note:1.hook: The word she had written was today's date — and a question mark.
note:1.line: 'This *note* is just for me,' Lin said, and tucked the book away.

probably:1.en: The morning fog sat low over the street. Lin walked past our store window without coming in, which she never does. She glanced at the sign, then at her watch. I thought she would *probably* come back later, but something about the way she walked made me feel less sure than usual.
probably:1.cnHint: 林一反常态地从店门口径直走过，我觉得她____有什么心事。
probably:1.hook: She looked back once, just before the fog swallowed her completely.
probably:1.line: 'You will *probably* understand soon enough,' she had said last night.

strategy:1.en: Lin spread a hand-drawn map on the hood of a parked car outside, pointing at streets and circling corners. She looked up, noticed me watching through the glass, and folded it in one fast move. Whatever her *strategy* was, it involved at least four blocks around our store. I felt a chill that had nothing to do with the wind.
strategy:1.cnHint: 林在店外研究一张地图，她的____显然和我们这条街有关。
strategy:1.hook: One of the circled spots on the map was exactly where I was standing.
strategy:1.line: 'A good *strategy* starts with knowing the ground,' Lin said with a smile.

building:1.en: Lin stood across the street, staring at the empty *building* next to ours — the one the Manager always said nobody wanted. She was measuring something with her eyes, stepping back, tilting her head. A real-estate agent appeared beside her and handed her a folder. My stomach dropped a little.
building:1.cnHint: 林盯着我们隔壁那栋空____，旁边还站着一个房产中介。
building:1.hook: The folder had a floor plan printed on the very first page.
building:1.line: 'That *building* has good light in the morning,' Lin told the agent calmly.

community:1.en: There was a small notice board at the corner where people pinned local news. Lin was adding a new flyer. I walked over after she left and read it: she was organising a *community* clean-up event — on our busiest Saturday morning. Every regular customer of ours had been personally invited by name.
community:1.cnHint: 林在街角公告栏贴出了一份活动通知，把我们最忙的那天变成了她的____活动。
community:1.hook: The last name on her invite list was mine.
community:1.line: 'A strong *community* is the best advertisement,' Lin said to no one in particular.

internet:1.en: I found Lin outside, sitting on an upturned crate, typing fast on her phone. She had set up a small mobile hotspot and was uploading something. She said the *internet* at her apartment was being cut off while they repaired the line, so she was borrowing the signal from the café down the road. The upload bar read ninety-nine percent.
internet:1.cnHint: 林借用附近的信号，用____上传一些东西，进度条已经快到头了。
internet:1.hook: The file name on her screen read 'grand-opening-date-FINAL.'
internet:1.line: 'The *internet* never sleeps, so neither do I,' Lin said without looking up.

seek:1.en: The street outside is quiet at 2 a.m., but Lin is already there, pacing slowly in front of our store. I watch through the glass door as she stops, looks up and down the road, and then walks in. She picks up a bottle of water and puts it back. She seems to *seek* something she cannot name. I decide to ask if she needs help.
seek:1.cnHint: 深夜，林在店外徘徊，似乎在____着什么说不清楚的东西。
seek:1.hook: She looks at me, opens her mouth, and says nothing.
seek:1.line: 'I always *seek* the right words, but they never come at night.'

exist:1.en: A cold wind pushes leaves past the door. Lin steps in from the street, shaking off the chill, and leans on the counter. She stares at the small lamp on the shelf. 'Does that lamp only *exist* for decoration?' she asks. I laugh and say it keeps the night from feeling too empty. She goes quiet, like the question meant more than she let on.
exist:1.cnHint: 林盯着架子上的小灯，问它是否只是为了装饰而____。
exist:1.hook: Her eyes do not leave the lamp even as she walks out.
exist:1.line: 'Some things only *exist* to remind you that someone cares.'

supply:1.en: Lin appears at the side door just before dawn, carrying a small box. She says the store down the block ran out of hot drinks and wonders if we have extra cups to share. I check our *supply* in the back room and find a whole shelf of them. I hand over twenty cups. She looks almost surprised that we said yes so quickly.
supply:1.cnHint: 林来借热饮杯子，我去库房查看了一下我们的____。
supply:1.hook: She pauses at the door and asks why we keep so many cups in stock.
supply:1.line: 'Our *supply* ran out an hour ago, so I thought I would try here.'

visit:1.en: Tang told me that Lin makes a *visit* to our store every Thursday night, always just before midnight. Tonight she arrives exactly on time, buys a small bag of nuts, and stands near the window watching the empty street. I refill the cup rack and keep one eye on her. There is something almost gentle about the way she watches the corner.
visit:1.cnHint: 同事告诉我，林每周四深夜都会来____一次。
visit:1.hook: Tonight, for the first time, she stays a full ten minutes past midnight.
visit:1.line: 'Every *visit* I tell myself it will be the last one, but here I am.'

worry:1.en: Just after three in the morning, Lin walks in looking pale. She buys a small bottle of juice and sits on the step outside the open door, sipping slowly. I wonder if I should say something. The *worry* on her face is quiet but clear, like a light left on in an empty room. After a while she stands, gives me a small nod, and leaves without a word.
worry:1.cnHint: 凌晨三点，林走进来，脸上带着明显的____。
worry:1.hook: She leaves a folded note on the step that I find only after she is gone.
worry:1.line: 'The *worry* goes away a little when I come here, honestly.'

adapt:1.en: Lin runs the small shop across the street. When our store started staying open later, she had to *adapt* too, keeping her own lights on until two in the morning. I see her yawning behind her counter through the window and feel a little guilty. Tonight she crosses the road and buys a coffee from us. We share a tired smile. Even rivals need to rest.
adapt:1.cnHint: 我们的店营业到更晚之后，林不得不____，也延长了自己的营业时间。
adapt:1.hook: She sips the coffee and says she has a question she has been holding for weeks.
adapt:1.line: 'I had to *adapt* to your new hours, so I may as well buy your coffee.'

bit:1.en: Lin drops in just after midnight and asks for change for the bus. I give her the coins and she looks down at them in her palm. 'A *bit* of luck would be nice tonight,' she says softly, almost to herself. I slide a small candy across the counter and tell her it is free. She raises an eyebrow but pockets it, then heads back out into the dark street.
bit:1.cnHint: 林说她今晚需要一____运气，我给了她一颗糖。
bit:1.hook: Twenty minutes later, she is back, and she is smiling this time.
bit:1.line: 'Just a *bit* of kindness goes a long way at this hour, you know.'

check:1.en: Lin crosses the street and comes in just before sunrise, pulling a small notebook from her pocket. She asks if she can *check* the price list on our wall. I say of course. She copies a few numbers down carefully and thanks me. I ask if she is doing research. She closes the notebook, tucks it away, and says only that she likes to keep her facts straight.
check:1.cnHint: 林进来仔细____了我们墙上的价格表，并把数字抄进了笔记本。
check:1.hook: She leaves the notebook behind, and her name is nowhere inside it.
check:1.line: 'I just need to *check* one thing, and then I will get out of your way.'

stick:1.en: Lin arrived at the store entrance before my shift even started, pressing a paper sign against the glass door. 'Special offer — our shop, not yours,' she said with a grin. The sign would not *stick* to the cold surface, sliding down again and again, but Lin refused to give up.
stick:1.cnHint: 林试图把一张宣传纸____在玻璃门上，但一直滑落。
stick:1.hook: The sign fell once more — and landed right at my feet.
stick:1.line: 'If this won't *stick*, I'll stand here and hold it all night.'

effective:1.en: Lin set up a small folding table just outside our store, handing out free samples of a new drink. The Manager watched from inside, arms crossed. 'Is that *effective*?' Tang whispered to me. We both looked — a line of curious people was already forming around Lin's table.
effective:1.cnHint: 林在店外摆摊派发试饮，Manager在想这是否____。
effective:1.hook: One of those curious people was our best regular customer.
effective:1.line: 'Free samples are the most *effective* trick I know.'

fear:1.en: A stray cat knocked over Lin's display stand on the pavement outside. Cans rolled everywhere. I ran out to help, and for a moment I saw real *fear* on Lin's face — not about the cans, but about the notebook that had fallen open among them. She snatched it up fast.
fear:1.cnHint: 一只流浪猫撞倒了林的展台，林脸上闪过一丝____。
fear:1.hook: That notebook had a list of names — and mine was near the top.
fear:1.line: 'Don't look at that — *fear* makes people do silly things, including me.'

hit:1.en: Lin was cycling past our store when her front wheel *hit* a crack in the pavement and she flew forward, landing on both palms. I grabbed the first-aid kit from under the counter and ran outside. She looked up, surprised, then quickly rearranged her expression into something more competitive.
hit:1.cnHint: 林骑车时撞上路面裂缝摔倒了，我跑出去帮忙。
hit:1.hook: She thanked me quietly — then asked to see our weekly sales numbers.
hit:1.line: 'I *hit* that crack because I was staring at your store window.'

assume:1.en: Lin leaned against the lamppost outside, watching our steady stream of late customers. 'You *assume* everyone walks in for convenience,' she told me, 'but they come for the light.' I looked back at the warm yellow glow of our windows on the dark street and found it hard to argue.
assume:1.cnHint: 林告诉我，不要____顾客进店只是为了方便。
assume:1.hook: She pulled out a small notebook and began writing something down.
assume:1.line: 'Don't *assume* you know why they choose your store over mine.'

generally:1.en: Lin stood at the corner, asking passers-by about their late-night shopping habits. Most people stopped for her clipboard. '*Generally*,' she announced to no one in particular, 'customers want three things: speed, warmth, and a friendly face.' She looked directly at me through the glass as she said it.
generally:1.cnHint: 林在路口做调查，总结出顾客____最看重的三件事。
generally:1.hook: Her third point landed harder than I expected it to.
generally:1.line: '*Generally* speaking, a smile keeps people coming back — just so you know.'

interaction:1.en: Lin was timing herself at the corner — counting how long each *interaction* with a passing stranger lasted before they walked away. She marked tallies on a small card with quick, neat strokes. When she noticed me watching from the doorway, she held up the card: fourteen seconds was her average.
interaction:1.cnHint: 林在路口记录每次与路人____的时长，发现平均只有十四秒。
interaction:1.hook: She then pointed her pen at me and clicked her stopwatch.
interaction:1.line: 'Every *interaction* is a chance — fourteen seconds is plenty of time.'

top:1.en: Lin climbed onto the low stone wall outside our store and taped a bright yellow banner to the *top* of her own shop sign across the street. It read: 'Open all night, just like them.' The Manager stepped outside, read it slowly, and then began to smile in a way that puzzled me.
top:1.cnHint: 林爬上矮墙，把横幅贴到对面店招牌的____上。
top:1.hook: The Manager's smile meant he already had an answer ready.
top:1.line: 'I put it on *top* so even you can't miss it tonight.'

consequence:1.en: The Manager called me outside just before my shift ended. 'Look at that,' he said, pointing to a pile of spilled boxes near the store entrance. A delivery had gone wrong, and the *consequence* was clear: the whole pavement was blocked. I grabbed a broom without being asked.
consequence:1.cnHint: 店长指着门口一堆乱箱子，这场失误的____让人头疼。
consequence:1.hook: Then I noticed Lin watching from across the street.
consequence:1.line: 'This is the *consequence* of rushing — clean it up before customers arrive.'

realize:1.en: I was sweeping the step outside when I saw Lin setting up a small stand just twenty metres away. At first I thought nothing of it. Then I began to *realize* she was selling the exact same drinks we carry inside. My broom stopped moving.
realize:1.cnHint: 我在门外扫地，慢慢____林在附近摆摊卖一样的饮料。
realize:1.hook: She caught my eye and smiled like she had been expecting me.
realize:1.line: 'Did you *realize* I was here all along, or did it just hit you?'

mostly:1.en: Our little corner store gets all kinds of visitors at night. They are *mostly* students from the university nearby, stopping in for hot noodles or a cold drink after late study. But tonight a man in a sharp suit stood outside, staring at the menu board like it was written in code.
mostly:1.cnHint: 夜里来店里的顾客____是附近的学生，但今晚来了一位奇怪的西装男。
mostly:1.hook: He asked for something we had quietly stopped selling last month.
mostly:1.line: 'Your late crowd is *mostly* students — that man is definitely not one.'

exactly:1.en: Lin crossed the street and stopped right in front of me. 'Your store closes at six in the morning,' she said. 'Mine opens at *exactly* six.' She tapped her watch with one finger, turned around, and walked back to her stand without waiting for my reply.
exactly:1.cnHint: 林走过来告诉我，她的摊子会在____六点我们打烊时开张。
exactly:1.hook: The Manager was standing just inside the door and had heard every word.
exactly:1.line: 'I open at *exactly* six — you do the math.'

vary:1.en: I asked Tang why our shelves looked different every few weeks. She laughed and leaned on the mop. 'Prices *vary* with the season, and the Manager moves things around to match.' Outside the window, Lin was rearranging her stand in the same thoughtful way.
vary:1.cnHint: 阿糖解释说店里的商品价格会____，林在窗外也在重新摆放她的货架。
vary:1.hook: Both of them seemed to be following the same unwritten rule.
vary:1.line: 'Prices *vary* — keep watching and you will see the pattern.'

brain:1.en: Tang pointed at Lin through the glass. 'Do not underestimate her,' she said quietly. 'That woman has a real *brain* for business. She once ran three stands at the same time and made a profit on all of them.' I looked at Lin tying a bright sign to her cart.
brain:1.cnHint: 阿糖提醒我不要小看林，说她有做生意的____，一人曾同时经营三个摊子。
brain:1.hook: Lin chose that moment to hang her sign directly opposite our window.
brain:1.line: 'She has a *brain* for this — she will outsell us if we blink.'

stress:1.en: The early morning delivery always came with *stress*: boxes stacked too high, the lift broken, and the driver already running late. Tang and I worked fast while Lin stood on the pavement opposite, watching calmly and sipping tea from a paper cup.
stress:1.cnHint: 早晨送货总是带来很多____，而林就在对面悠闲地喝茶看热闹。
stress:1.hook: When we finally finished, Lin gave us a slow, friendly clap.
stress:1.line: 'All that *stress* over boxes — I just paid someone else to carry mine.'

financial:1.en: The Manager spread a sheet of numbers on the counter and slid it toward me. 'This is our *financial* record for the past three months,' he said. 'Study it tonight.' Through the window I could see Lin counting coins at her stand with a very satisfied look.
financial:1.cnHint: 店长把最近三个月的____报表递给我，让我好好研究。
financial:1.hook: Two of those months showed a dip that matched exactly when Lin arrived.
financial:1.line: 'Our *financial* record tells the truth — someone out there is very clever.'

easily:1.en: The rain started without warning. I grabbed a stack of umbrellas from the back shelf and ran outside to sell them from the doorway. Lin appeared across the street, already setting up her own umbrella stand. She had *easily* twice as many as I did, all lined up in bright colours.
easily:1.cnHint: 突然下起雨来，我冲到门口卖伞，林在街对面____摆出了两倍多的伞。
easily:1.hook: She caught my eye and smiled, and it was not a friendly smile.
easily:1.line: 'I *easily* sold out last week — how many do you have?'

protect:1.en: A sudden wind swept down the street, knocking over the small sign the Manager had placed outside. I caught it just in time and propped it against the wall, leaning my back against it to *protect* it from the next gust. Lin walked past, glanced at me, and said nothing.
protect:1.cnHint: 一阵大风把店外的招牌吹倒，我用身体____它不再被风吹走。
protect:1.hook: She paused at the corner and looked back, as if she was waiting for the sign to fall again.
protect:1.line: 'You have to *protect* the sign — the Manager checks it every morning.'

advantage:1.en: Lin ran the convenience store one block away. She opened thirty minutes earlier than us each day, which gave her a real *advantage* — she caught every commuter rushing for the first train. I stood outside counting heads as they all turned into her door instead of ours.
advantage:1.cnHint: 林的店比我们早开半小时，这个时间上的____让她抢到了每一位早班通勤客。
advantage:1.hook: I pulled out a notepad and started writing down every bus and train time I could remember.
advantage:1.line: 'Opening early is my biggest *advantage* — and I worked hard for it.'

break:1.en: At half past two in the morning, the street was finally empty. I stepped outside for a short *break*, leaning against the wall with a warm can of tea. The night air smelled of rain and fried food. Then I heard the bell above Lin's door ring — she had a late customer too.
break:1.cnHint: 凌晨两点半，街道安静下来，我出去稍作____，却听见林的店门铃也响了。
break:1.hook: Whoever walked into her store at this hour was carrying something large under one arm.
break:1.line: 'Even a five-minute *break* out here is the best part of the night shift.'

conclude:1.en: After a week of watching the foot traffic outside both stores, I sat down with my notebook. More people stopped to read our window signs, but then walked on to Lin's. From this, I could only *conclude* that her prices were lower — or her snacks were simply better than ours.
conclude:1.cnHint: 观察了一周的客流后，我只能____：大家宁愿多走一步去林的店。
conclude:1.hook: Tomorrow I was going to walk in there and buy every snack she sold.
conclude:1.line: 'I *conclude* from the numbers that she changed her prices last Monday.'

figure:1.en: I was trying to understand the weekly sales sheet the Manager had left me when Lin appeared in our doorway, dry from the drizzle outside. She glanced at the paper in my hands and raised an eyebrow. The *figure* at the bottom of the column was embarrassingly small and she clearly saw it.
figure:1.cnHint: 林出现在门口，一眼瞥见我手里销售表最下方那个难看的____。
figure:1.hook: She pressed her lips together, said nothing, and bought a single piece of gum.
figure:1.line: 'That *figure* does not even cover your electricity bill, does it?'

fit:1.en: The Manager had bought a new outdoor display rack and asked me to set it up before the morning rush. No matter how I turned the pieces, they would not *fit* together neatly. Lin jogged past on her morning run, stopped, looked at the mess on the pavement, and crouched down beside me.
fit:1.cnHint: 我怎么拼都无法让新展架的零件____在一起，林晨跑路过，蹲下来看了看。
fit:1.hook: She picked up one piece, clicked it into place in two seconds, and stood up without a word.
fit:1.line: 'These bolts *fit* the left side first — you were starting from the wrong end.'

particular:1.en: The Manager had told me to keep a *particular* shelf near the door stocked at all times — the one holding hot drinks and pocket tissues. 'Customers decide in three seconds,' he said. I understood when I saw Lin's store: that exact same shelf sat right beside her entrance, always full, always tidy.
particular:1.cnHint: 店长叮嘱我要随时保持门口____那排货架的库存，我发现林的店里也有一模一样的设置。
particular:1.hook: I wondered who had taught them both the same trick — and who had taught it first.
particular:1.line: 'That *particular* shelf is the first thing every customer sees when they walk in.'

fruit:1.en: Lin showed up at the store entrance just before my shift ended, holding a paper bag. 'I picked these from my uncle's garden,' she said, setting three ripe peaches on the counter. The sweet smell filled the whole store. Each *fruit* had a small red sticker on it that I did not recognise. I wondered what the sticker meant.
fruit:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在清晨带来了自家园子里摘的____，放在收银台上，贴纸上有些神秘。
fruit:1.hook: That small red sticker was not from any garden I knew.
fruit:1.line: 'Each *fruit* comes from a very old tree — taste one and you will understand.'

waste:1.en: Lin stood outside under the streetlight, staring at a row of rice boxes the Manager had set out for disposal. 'It hurts to watch,' she said quietly. I stepped out to stand beside her. We both knew the store could not sell food past its time, but it still felt wrong to *waste* so many good meals on a quiet Tuesday night.
waste:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在店外看着一排即将被丢掉的饭盒，觉得这样____太可惜了。
waste:1.hook: Then Lin pulled out her phone and started dialling someone.
waste:1.line: 'I hate to *waste* good food — I know people who would love this tonight.'

learning:1.en: I found Lin outside the store, sitting on the low wall with a notebook open on her knee. She was reading English words aloud, very softly. 'Night shifts are good for *learning*,' she told me, not looking up. I leaned against the door and listened. Her voice was steady and calm, like someone who had already decided to win.
learning:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在店外夜读，说深夜很适合____，她的语气让人印象深刻。
learning:1.hook: But the notebook was not an English textbook at all.
learning:1.line: 'Quiet streets are the best place for *learning* — no one bothers you out here.'

manager:1.en: Lin was waiting on the pavement when the early delivery van pulled up. She greeted the driver before I could even get the door open. 'She acts like the *manager* already,' Tang whispered to me from behind the register. I laughed, but I also noticed how the driver handed Lin the clipboard first, without thinking twice.
manager:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在店门外抢先接收货物，阿糖悄声说她举止像个____。
manager:1.hook: The driver seemed to know Lin from somewhere other than this street.
manager:1.line: 'If you want to be a *manager* one day, start by showing up before everyone else.'

knowledge:1.en: Outside the store, Lin stopped a lost tourist who was studying a paper map. Without hesitation she gave clear directions in both English and the local language. I watched from the window, impressed. Her *knowledge* of every alley and shortcut in this neighbourhood was something the Manager had mentioned before, but seeing it was different.
knowledge:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在店外帮迷路的游客指路，她对街区的____让人叹服。
knowledge:1.hook: The tourist thanked her and then asked her something that made Lin go very still.
knowledge:1.line: '*Knowledge* of the streets around here has saved me more than once at night.'

mental:1.en: I stepped outside for a breath of air and found Lin doing slow stretches on the pavement. 'Long shifts get heavy,' she said. 'Not just the body — the *mental* part is harder.' I nodded. She rolled her neck, looked up at the sky, and smiled like she had just solved something. I went back inside feeling unexpectedly lighter.
mental:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在店外做伸展运动，说长班次对____状态的消耗比身体更大。
mental:1.hook: She had mentioned a 'long shift,' but Lin did not work the night shift here.
mental:1.line: 'The *mental* load of this job is real — you have to find your own way to reset.'

weight:1.en: The delivery crates arrived at the side entrance just as Lin was passing by. She stopped, watched the new clerk — me — struggle with the largest box, then reached over and lifted one end without asking. 'You take the back,' she said simply. Together we moved it inside easily. The *weight* had felt impossible alone, and effortless together.
weight:1.cnHint: 林帮我一起搬沉重的货箱，两个人分担____就轻松多了。
weight:1.hook: She knew exactly which shelf that crate belonged on without being told.
weight:1.line: 'The *weight* is not the problem — the angle is. Shift it a little and it moves.'

academic:1.en: Lin was reading a printed notice posted on the wall outside the store. It advertised a free evening talk at the nearby university. 'Are you going?' I asked. She shrugged. 'I like the ideas, but the language is too stiff.' She traced one line with her finger. 'Why does *academic* writing always sound like it is trying to push you away?'
academic:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林看着大学讲座的海报，抱怨____写作的语言总是让人望而生畏。
academic:1.hook: The name at the bottom of the notice was one Lin clearly recognised.
academic:1.line: '*Academic* talk is fine in a classroom, but out here plain words work better.'

major:1.en: Lin showed up outside at midnight, staring at our store window with her arms crossed. She worked at the small shop across the street. The *major* reason she kept coming over, she later admitted, was that our coffee smelled better. Tonight, though, she just stood there, not coming in.
major:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林站在店外盯着橱窗，后来承认她总来这里的____原因是咖啡香气。
major:1.hook: She pressed a folded note against the glass and walked away.
major:1.line: 'The *major* problem is your coffee smells too good from across the street.'

communication:1.en: The street outside was empty except for an old man talking to a cat near the lamp post. I watched through the window. He paused, tilted his head, and nodded, as if the cat had answered. Real *communication*, Tang said beside me, takes many forms. The cat then walked into our store.
communication:1.cnHint: 老人在路灯下与猫交流，阿糖说真正的____形式多样。
communication:1.hook: The cat jumped straight onto the counter and sat beside the register.
communication:1.line: 'That is real *communication* — better than most people I know.'

market:1.en: Every Saturday, a small street *market* opened one block away, and the smell of fresh fruit drifted all the way to our door. Customers came in smiling, bags in hand, and bought cold drinks without even checking the price. The old woman who sold peaches always stopped here last, just before dawn.
market:1.cnHint: 街边____每周六开市，桃子摊的老奶奶总在天亮前最后一个来到店里。
market:1.hook: Last Saturday, she arrived with two peaches and no money, only a quiet smile.
market:1.line: 'The *market* closes at five, so I always save the last peaches for you.'

apply:1.en: A young man stood under the lamp outside, reading a paper form in the cold wind. He came in and asked to borrow a pen. He needed to *apply* for a night-school place and the deadline was tomorrow morning. I found him a pen, and he sat on the step outside, writing carefully under the store light.
apply:1.cnHint: 一个年轻人在店外借笔，要在天亮前____夜校名额。
apply:1.hook: He slid the finished form under a closed office door just as the clock struck five.
apply:1.line: 'I have to *apply* before dawn or I lose my chance completely.'

per:1.en: Lin taped a small sign to the lamp post outside our store: 'Hot soup: five yuan *per* cup.' She had set up a tiny folding table on the pavement. The Manager watched from the window, quietly impressed. Her line of customers stretched almost to our door before nine o'clock.
per:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在店外路灯旁摆摊卖热汤，每杯五元，队伍几乎排到我们门口。
per:1.hook: Then she ran out of soup and pointed every customer straight at us.
per:1.line: 'Five yuan *per* cup — cheapest hot thing on this street tonight.'

treat:1.en: A little girl stood outside with her grandfather, both looking at the snack shelf through the glass. He had exactly enough coins for one item. She pointed at a small bag of crackers for him, not for herself. The way she looked after him was a *treat* to watch. He bought two bags anyway.
treat:1.cnHint: 小女孩指着饼干要给爷爷买，她照顾老人的方式真是一种____。
treat:1.hook: As they left, the grandfather slipped a second bag into her coat pocket.
treat:1.line: 'Watching those two is a real *treat* — better than anything on TV.'

creative:1.en: Tang spotted a teenager drawing on the pavement outside with chalk, turning the cracks in the ground into a map of an imaginary city. 'Very *creative*,' Tang said, leaning out the door. The kid looked up, surprised anyone noticed. He came in, bought a juice, and left a tiny chalk arrow pointing at our entrance.
creative:1.cnHint: 一个少年在店外用粉笔画地图，阿糖夸他很____，他随后在门口留下了指向箭头。
creative:1.hook: The next morning, the chalk city had grown to cover the whole corner.
creative:1.line: 'That is the most *creative* thing I have seen on this street all year.'

perform:1.en: Two students rehearsed a short skit on the pavement across from our store, using a lamp post as their stage prop. They asked me to watch and tell them if they were loud enough. The taller one forgot his line, laughed, and then *performed* it perfectly on the second try. A passing cyclist stopped to clap.
perform:1.cnHint: 两个学生在店外路灯下排练小品，高个子第二次____得非常完美。
perform:1.hook: They asked if they could rehearse here every Thursday night.
perform:1.line: 'I finally *performed* that line right — did it sound okay from inside?'

prepare:1.en: Lin showed up outside at midnight, spreading papers on the hood of a parked bicycle. I watched through the glass as she used a small light to *prepare* a handwritten sign, each word written with surprising care. She pressed the finished sign against our window — it read: BETTER SNACKS NEXT DOOR. Then she winked at me.
prepare:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在店外____着一块手写广告牌，对着我们的橱窗贴了上去。
prepare:1.hook: The address on her sign was for a store that closed two years ago.
prepare:1.line: 'I always *prepare* my signs by hand — machines can't match the personal touch.'

workplace:1.en: Lin leaned against the lamp-post outside, arms folded, studying our storefront the way a doctor studies a patient. 'Your *workplace* needs better lighting,' she called out when I stepped outside to restock the bin. She wasn't wrong. The left bulb had been flickering for a week.
workplace:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林站在店外，对我们的____评头论足，但她说的话倒也没错。
workplace:1.hook: She already knew about the broken bulb before I mentioned it.
workplace:1.line: 'A tidy *workplace* tells customers everything they need to know about you.'

post:1.en: Lin stood beneath the corner street-light, reaching up to *post* a small paper notice on the public board next to our door. I read it from inside: FREE TEA WITH EVERY PURCHASE — COMPETITOR STORE. She smoothed it flat with one careful hand, then glanced back at me with a polite smile.
post:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林在我们门口的公告栏上____了一张竞争对手的优惠通知。
post:1.hook: Below her notice, half-hidden, was one that looked exactly like it from last week.
post:1.line: 'I *post* a new notice every Tuesday — consistency is everything in this business.'

complete:1.en: Lin appeared at our window at 2 a.m. with a clipboard, ticking boxes with great focus. She told me she was running a survey of every corner store on the street. Ours was the last. 'Now I can *complete* my report,' she said, clicking her pen shut with a satisfied snap.
complete:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林拿着写字板在做调查，我们是最后一家，终于让她____了报告。
complete:1.hook: She tucked the clipboard away before I could read a single question on it.
complete:1.line: 'Just one more answer and I can *complete* the whole survey tonight.'

measure:1.en: Lin stood outside with a small tape in hand, carefully trying to *measure* the width of our store's front window. She wrote numbers in a little notebook, frowned, then measured again. I knocked on the glass. She looked up and gave a cheerful thumbs-up, as if this were perfectly ordinary.
measure:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林拿着卷尺在店外____我们橱窗的宽度，还认真地记了下来。
measure:1.hook: Her notebook already had three other pages filled with numbers I couldn't read.
measure:1.line: 'I like to *measure* everything before I make a single decision — that's just good sense.'

recommend:1.en: A tired student stopped Lin outside and asked where to buy a warm drink at this hour. I expected her to point down the street. Instead, she paused, looked at our lit window, and said something I couldn't quite hear. The student walked straight through our door. 'She said to *recommend* you,' he told me, looking puzzled.
recommend:1.cnHint: 一个学生问隔壁咖啡店的林去哪买热饮，她竟然把对方____到了我们店里。
recommend:1.hook: Lin was already gone by the time I looked back through the window.
recommend:1.line: 'I only *recommend* a place if I honestly think it deserves it — even a rival.'

resource:1.en: Lin knocked on the glass at 3 a.m. and held up a hand-drawn map of every store on the block, colour-coded by product type. 'Information is the most important *resource* in retail,' she said through the gap in the door, then rolled the map up neatly and walked away into the dark.
resource:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林带来了一张手绘街区地图，说信息是零售业最重要的____。
resource:1.hook: Our store was marked on her map with a small gold star.
resource:1.line: 'Time is a *resource* — I never waste a single night shift's worth of it.'

specific:1.en: Lin slid a folded note under our door just after 4 a.m. Inside was a list of six items, each with a *specific* time of day and the number of customers who had asked for them. Hot soup: 11 p.m., four people. Fresh bread: 5 a.m., seven people. No explanation. Just the facts, in very neat handwriting.
specific:1.cnHint: 隔壁咖啡店的林塞来一张便条，上面列出了顾客在____时间段内最想买的商品。
specific:1.hook: Every item on her list was something we had been out of stock for a month.
specific:1.line: 'Be *specific* about what customers want — guessing is just polite failure.'

trouble:1.en: Outside the store, Lin was arguing with a delivery driver over a box of misrouted goods. I stepped onto the pavement to listen. 'This happens every week,' Tang whispered behind me. The driver looked ready to leave without signing anything. Real *trouble* was about to begin.
trouble:1.cnHint: 林在店门外和送货司机因为货物弄错地址发生了____。
trouble:1.hook: The driver's hand moved toward his phone.
trouble:1.line: 'This *trouble* started long before you showed up tonight.'

reflect:1.en: Lin stood outside under the yellow streetlight after the argument ended. She did not move for a long time. I watched her face *reflect* the quiet uncertainty that comes after a fight you are not sure you won. Tang simply handed her a warm can of tea and said nothing.
reflect:1.cnHint: 争吵结束后，林在路灯下静静地____着刚才发生的事。
reflect:1.hook: Then Lin looked up and smiled — but not at Tang.
reflect:1.line: 'I need a moment to *reflect* before I say another word.'

attend:1.en: A handwritten notice was taped to the lamp post near our door. It announced a neighbourhood meeting that everyone on the street was expected to *attend*. Lin read it twice, then pulled it down and tucked it in her jacket. I pretended not to notice, but Tang definitely did.
attend:1.cnHint: 街边路灯上贴着一张通知，提醒附近居民____一个社区会议。
attend:1.hook: Lin folded the notice so the date was hidden.
attend:1.line: 'We should all *attend*, unless someone has a reason not to.'

belief:1.en: Lin leaned against the wall outside, arms folded, watching the empty street. 'You look like you lost something,' I said. She shook her head. 'Just testing a *belief*,' she said quietly. 'I thought people came out more at night. Turns out they really do stay home.' She seemed almost pleased by that.
belief:1.cnHint: 林靠墙站在外面，说她在验证一个关于夜晚行人的____。
belief:1.hook: She then took out a small notebook and wrote something down.
belief:1.line: 'It is a *belief* I have held since I started this job.'

carry:1.en: Two large bags of unsold bread sat by the store entrance, meant for the morning food van. Lin walked past and, without a word, picked them both up. 'You do not have to do that,' I told her. 'Somebody has to *carry* them,' she said, stepping into the cool night air alone.
carry:1.cnHint: 店门口有两袋没卖完的面包，林默默地____着它们走进了夜里。
carry:1.hook: She turned left at the corner — the van parks on the right.
carry:1.line: 'I will *carry* these myself — no need to follow me.'

else:1.en: A stranger stopped outside and pressed his face against the glass, studying the shelves for a long time. He came in, looked at every aisle, and bought nothing. On his way out he asked, 'Is there anywhere *else* nearby that sells dried plums?' Lin, standing outside, pointed firmly in the opposite direction from the actual shop.
else:1.cnHint: 一个陌生人问附近还有没有____的地方卖话梅，林给他指了一个奇怪的方向。
else:1.hook: The stranger thanked her and walked straight into the dark alley.
else:1.line: 'Nowhere *else* on this street will give you a better price.'

policy:2.en: Lin walked in just before midnight and pointed at the sign above the register. 'Your return *policy* says three days,' she said, placing a receipt on the counter. I checked the sign. She was right. The Manager had never mentioned this rule to me, not once.
policy:2.cnHint: 林指着收银台上方的牌子，要求按照____退货。
policy:2.hook: The receipt was dated four months ago.
policy:2.line: 'Your return *policy* says three days, so I am here on day two.'

industry:2.en: Lin pulled out a thick notebook and set it on the magazine shelf beside me. 'I am studying the convenience store *industry*,' she said, clicking her pen. She wrote something, glanced at the snack display, then wrote again. I felt like a fish being watched in a glass bowl.
industry:2.cnHint: 林拿出笔记本，声称自己在研究便利店____。
industry:2.hook: She turned the notebook so I could not see the page.
industry:2.line: 'The convenience store *industry* is full of small secrets, you know.'

concern:2.en: Tang found the note first. It was tucked under the milk crates in the back room. The handwriting was neat, the message short: 'Your pricing is my *concern*.' No name, no date. Tang held it up to the light as if extra brightness might reveal more. It did not.
concern:2.cnHint: 唐在库房发现一张纸条，内容让他感到一丝____。
concern:2.hook: The ink was still faintly wet.
concern:2.line: 'This pricing is a serious *concern*, and someone wants us to know it.'

present:2.en: A small box sat on the step outside the store at 2 a.m. I carried it inside. No ribbon, no card, just plain brown paper. Whatever was *present* inside made a soft sound when I tilted it, like sand shifting. I set it on the counter and did not open it.
present:2.cnHint: 凌晨两点，我在门口发现了一个没有标签的____。
present:2.hook: Lin arrived ten minutes later and looked straight at the box.
present:2.line: 'Is there a *present* on the counter, or am I dreaming at this hour?'

claim:2.en: Lin stood at the lost-and-found box and lifted out a blue umbrella. 'I *claim* this,' she said simply. I asked for a description. She gave one — correct colour, broken middle spoke, small dent in the handle. I handed it over. She smiled, which was somehow more suspicious than a frown.
claim:2.cnHint: 林走到失物招领箱旁，____了一把蓝色雨伞。
claim:2.hook: The umbrella had been there since before I started working.
claim:2.line: 'I *claim* this umbrella; it has been waiting here long enough.'

half:2.en: I found *half* a paper map in the recycling bin behind the register. The missing side had been torn away cleanly. The remaining half showed only local streets and a single red circle with no label. Tang said he had never seen it before. I believed him about the map.
half:2.cnHint: 我在回收箱里发现了一张地图的____，上面画有一个红圈。
half:2.hook: The red circle was exactly where our store stood.
half:2.line: 'Only *half* a map — whoever left this kept the useful part.'

successful:2.en: Lin taped a small flyer to the window near the door. It read: 'Be *successful* — shop smarter.' Below the words was a tiny arrow pointing to the store across the street. I peeled the flyer off before the Manager arrived. Lin was already gone. The window was still warm where the tape had been.
successful:2.cnHint: 林在橱窗上贴了一张传单，暗示去别处购物才能____。
successful:2.hook: There were three more flyers folded in my jacket pocket.
successful:2.line: 'To be *successful*, a smart shopper always compares prices first.'

access:2.en: The back-room door had a new keypad. The Manager had changed the code without telling anyone. Tang tried four combinations. I tried two. Neither of us could get *access* to the stockroom where all the next-day delivery boxes were waiting. We sold the last bottle of water at 3 a.m.
access:2.cnHint: 库房门换了密码锁，我们无法____里面的货物。
access:2.hook: Lin walked in holding a small piece of paper with numbers on it.
access:2.line: 'Without *access* to the stockroom, we cannot restock anything tonight.'

positive:2.en: Behind the counter, I found a folded note tucked under the register. It was from Lin, the clerk at the shop across the street. The words were sharp at first, but the final line surprised me: 'Stay *positive*. This street is big enough for both of us.'
positive:2.cnHint: 我在收银台下发现林留下的纸条，语气出乎意料地____。
positive:2.hook: But why had Lin left it there at all?
positive:2.line: 'Stay *positive* — this street is big enough for both of us.'

economic:2.en: A folded newspaper sat on the delivery shelf, left by Lin. The headline circled in red pen read: LOCAL SHOPS FACE *ECONOMIC* PRESSURE AS CHAIN STORES MOVE IN. A short note in the margin said, 'This affects us both. Think about it.'
economic:2.cnHint: 林留下一份报纸，上面圈出了关于小店面临____压力的新闻。
economic:2.hook: Someone had already underlined our store's address in blue.
economic:2.line: 'The *economic* pressure out there is real — we should talk.'

link:2.en: Inside a returned umbrella left at our door, I found a folded map. A red line connected our store to Lin's shop across the street, with a small note: 'There is a *link* between us whether you see it or not. Same suppliers. Same customers.'
link:2.cnHint: 一把雨伞里藏着一张地图，画出了我们两家店之间的____。
link:2.hook: The handwriting matched the note under the register.
link:2.line: 'There is a *link* between us — same suppliers, same customers.'

produce:2.en: A small crate appeared outside our back door before dawn. It held six apples and a card: 'My cousin's farm can *produce* more than my shop needs. Take some. No charge.' The card had no name, but the handwriting was Lin's.
produce:2.cnHint: 天亮前，林悄悄在我们后门放下了一箱她表弟农场____的苹果。
produce:2.hook: Six apples seemed like a small peace offering — or a test.
produce:2.line: 'My cousin's farm can *produce* more than one small shop needs.'

teach:2.en: Pinned to our bulletin board was a printed flyer, edges still warm from the printer. It offered a free workshop: LEARN TO SPOT EXPIRED GOODS. At the bottom, in careful handwriting: 'I will *teach* the class myself. — Lin.' The Manager had never mentioned this.
teach:2.cnHint: 布告栏上出现了一张林亲手写的传单，说她愿意来____大家辨别过期商品。
teach:2.hook: The Manager's silence on the matter was loud enough to hear.
teach:2.line: 'I will *teach* the class myself — no charge, just show up.'

worth:2.en: Lin slipped a folded receipt under our door. On the back she had written a price list comparing our goods to hers. At the bottom: 'Honest prices are *worth* more than a loyalty card.' I stared at it for a long moment.
worth:2.cnHint: 林塞来一张收据，背面写着对比价目表，暗示诚实定价才____更多。
worth:2.hook: Her numbers were uncomfortably close to correct.
worth:2.line: 'Honest prices are *worth* more than any loyalty card, trust me.'

common:2.en: The morning delivery brought an extra box addressed to both stores. Inside was a handwritten letter: 'We share the same street, the same regulars, the same worries. That is *common* ground. We could build something on it.' No return address. Just Lin's small, neat signature.
common:2.cnHint: 一个寄给两家店的包裹送来，林在信里说我们有____的处境和顾客。
common:2.hook: Tang quietly folded the letter and slipped it into a pocket.
common:2.line: 'That is *common* ground — we could actually build something on it.'

daily:2.en: A small chalkboard appeared overnight, leaning against our store window from outside. It listed the *daily* specials — but they were Lin's specials, not ours. At the bottom, chalk still bright: 'Swap boards? Customers see both. Everyone wins.' I had not agreed to anything yet.
daily:2.cnHint: 林把写着她家____特价商品的小黑板悄悄靠在了我们店的橱窗外。
daily:2.hook: The Manager arrived early that morning, and he was smiling.
daily:2.line: 'Let us swap *daily* boards — customers see both, everyone wins.'

explain:2.en: Lin slid a folded note across the counter at 2 a.m. I unfolded it to find a hand-drawn map of the back storeroom, with arrows and small labels. Before I could speak, Lin tapped the note and said I needed to *explain* this to Tang by morning. The map showed a hidden shelf none of us knew existed.
explain:2.cnHint: 林深夜递给我一张手绘地图，要我在早上之前把它____给唐。
explain:2.hook: Why did Lin know about a shelf the Manager never mentioned?
explain:2.line: 'Can you *explain* to Tang exactly where that shelf is?'

examine:2.en: A small package arrived just after midnight, addressed to the store in handwriting I did not recognize. I set it on the counter and began to *examine* every side carefully, turning it slowly under the light. No return address. No stamp. Tang walked in, took one look, and told me not to open it yet.
examine:2.cnHint: 午夜后一个来历不明的包裹出现在柜台上，我仔细____了每一面。
examine:2.hook: Tang knew something about that package, and was not ready to share it.
examine:2.line: '*Examine* every corner before you do anything else.'

influence:2.en: Lin always bought the same two items on Tuesday nights. This week Lin stood in the snack aisle for ten quiet minutes, then chose something completely different. Tang nudged me and whispered that the new display I had built seemed to *influence* even the most loyal regulars. I felt oddly proud — until I noticed Lin looked a little troubled.
influence:2.cnHint: 林平时购物习惯固定，但我新布置的货架陈列似乎____了林的选择。
influence:2.hook: Whatever was on Lin's mind that night had nothing to do with snacks.
influence:2.line: 'A good display can *influence* people more than they realise.'

argue:2.en: I heard raised voices near the drinks fridge just before three in the morning. Lin and Tang had found the same last bottle of cold barley tea and were starting to *argue* over it in loud, fast whispers so as not to wake the street. I walked over slowly, holding a second bottle I had just found in the back. Both of them stopped and stared.
argue:2.cnHint: 林和唐在饮料柜前小声____起来，原来只剩最后一瓶大麦茶了。
argue:2.hook: The look the two of them shared after that was harder to read than the argument.
argue:2.line: 'There is no need to *argue* — I found another one just now.'

pass:2.en: Every night at exactly half past two, an elderly man in a long coat would *pass* the glass door, slow his steps, glance at the light inside, and then walk on without entering. He had done this every night since my first shift. Tonight, for the first time, he stopped.
pass:2.cnHint: 每天深夜都有一位老人____过店门口，今晚他第一次停下了脚步。
pass:2.hook: One hand rose to the door handle, then went still.
pass:2.line: 'Does anyone *pass* here every night around this time?'

serious:2.en: The Manager called me at one in the morning, which had never happened before. The voice on the phone was low and *serious*, asking me to check whether the back door was locked. I checked — it was fine. But the Manager stayed on the line for another full minute without saying anything else.
serious:2.cnHint: 店长深夜打来电话，语气十分____，只让我去确认后门是否锁好了。
serious:2.hook: Someone had been at that door, and the Manager already knew.
serious:2.line: 'This is *serious* — please check the back door right now.'

despite:2.en: Lin arrived soaking wet at quarter to three, *despite* the fact that I could see a folded umbrella sticking out of Lin's bag. Lin bought a hot drink, sat on the small step near the window, and stared at the rain without a word. After a while Lin smiled at nothing in particular, dried off a little, and left the umbrella behind on purpose.
despite:2.cnHint: 林淋着雨走进来，____包里就有一把伞，却故意没用。
despite:2.hook: The umbrella had someone else's name written on the handle.
despite:2.line: 'I walked in the rain *despite* having an umbrella — do not ask why.'

express:2.en: Tang slipped a folded piece of paper into the suggestion box near the door, then pretended to tidy a shelf nearby. I was curious, so I waited until Tang left, opened the box, and found the note on top. It was one sentence long, a careful attempt to *express* something to the Manager that Tang had clearly never been able to say out loud. I folded it back and closed the box.
express:2.cnHint: 唐悄悄往意见箱里塞了一张纸条，想借此____一些平时说不出口的话。
express:2.hook: The sentence on that note would have surprised the Manager very much.
express:2.line: "'It is easier to *express* something in writing than face to face.'

determine:2.en: A folded note had been left under the counter, addressed to no one. I opened it slowly, trying to *determine* what it meant. The handwriting was neat, the message short: 'The third shelf on the left. Check before midnight.' I looked up. Lin was watching from across the street, arms folded.
determine:2.cnHint: 柜台下有一张纸条，我想____它的含义，林正在街对面注视着我。
determine:2.hook: The third shelf held something no one had stocked.
determine:2.line: 'I need to *determine* who left this note before the Manager finds it.'
